sentences.zh: 石勒

translations.literal: Shi Le
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le

sentences.zh: 石勒字世龍，初名㔨，上黨武鄉羯人也。

translations.literal: Shi Le styled Shilong; originally his name was Bei, and he was a Jie man from Wuxiang in Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le, courtesy name Shilong and originally named Bei, was a Jie from Wuxiang in Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 其先匈奴別部羌渠之胄。

translations.literal: His ancestors were of a separate branch of the Xiongnu, the descendants of Qiangqu.
translations.idiomatic: His line sprang from Qiangqu, a distinct division among the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 祖耶奕-{于}-，父周曷-{朱}-，一名乞冀加，並為部落小率。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Ye Yiyu; his father was Zhou Hezhu, also called Qijijia; both were petty commanders of the tribe.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ye Yiyu and his father Zhou Hezhu—also known as Qijijia—had both been minor tribal officers.

sentences.zh: 勒生時赤光滿室，白氣自天屬-{于}-中庭，見者咸異之。

translations.literal: When Le was born, red light filled the chamber, and white vapour from Heaven reached to the middle courtyard; all who saw it thought it strange.
translations.idiomatic: At his birth the room blazed with red light, and a shaft of white mist ran from the sky down into the courtyard; everyone who saw it took it for a prodigy.

sentences.zh: 年十四，隨邑人行販洛陽，倚嘯上東門，王衍見而異之，顧謂左右曰：「向者胡雛，吾觀其聲視有奇志，恐將為天下之患。

translations.literal: At age fourteen he followed people of the town travelling to peddle goods in Luoyang; leaning against the wall he whistled at the upper east gate. Wang Yan saw him and thought him strange, turned to those at his left and right and said, "That Hu youngster a moment ago—I observe in his voice and look an unusual ambition; I fear he will become a scourge to all under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he joined townsfolk hawking goods in Luoyang and, lounging by the Upper East Gate, gave a long whistle. Wang Yan noticed him, found him unsettling, and said quietly to his attendants, "That young barbarian we just passed—there is something fierce in how he carries himself. Left unchecked, he will become a danger to the realm."

sentences.zh: 」馳遣收之，會勒已去。

translations.literal: He sent riders in haste to seize him, but it happened that Le had already gone.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan sent riders to seize him at once, but Shi Le had already slipped away.

sentences.zh: 長而壯健有膽力，雄武好騎射。

translations.literal: Growing up he was stalwart and daring, bold in war and fond of horseback archery.
translations.idiomatic: As a man he was powerfully built and fearless, warlike and devoted to riding and shooting.

sentences.zh: 曷-{朱}-性凶粗，不為羣胡所附，每使勒代己督攝，部胡愛信之。

translations.literal: Hezhu by nature was fierce and crude and not attached to by the herd of Hu; he always made Le act in his stead to oversee and control them; the Hu of the department loved and trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Hezhu was violent and uncouth, and the other Hu would not follow him; he habitually left Shi Le to supervise the band in his place, and the tribesmen came to love and trust Shi Le instead.

sentences.zh: 所居武鄉北原山下草木皆有鐵騎之象，家園中生人參，花葉甚茂，悉成人狀。

translations.literal: Where he dwelt, north of the plain below Mount Yuan at Wuxiang, the grass and trees all had the appearance of armoured horsemen; in the garden at home ginseng sprouted, its flowers and leaves very lush, all shaped like human forms.
translations.idiomatic: North of the Yuan foothills at Wuxiang, every tree and blade of grass seemed to silhouette mailed riders; in the family plot ginseng sprang up so thick that its leaves looked like tiny human figures.

sentences.zh: 父老及相者皆曰：「此胡狀貌奇異，志度非常，其終不可量也。

translations.literal: The elders and physiognomists all said, "This Hu's appearance is strange; his intent and bearing are not ordinary—his end cannot be fathomed."
translations.idiomatic: Elders and fortune-tellers said to one another, "That foreign lad's features are uncanny, and his bearing is unlike anyone else's—who can say how far he may rise?"

sentences.zh: 」勸邑人厚遇之。

translations.literal: They urged the townspeople to treat him generously.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed the community to show him real generosity.

sentences.zh: 時多嗤笑，唯鄔人郭敬、陽曲甯驅以為信然，並加資贍。

translations.literal: At the time many sneered and laughed; only Guo Jing of Wu and Ning Qu of Yangqu thought it was truly so, and together they supplied funds.
translations.idiomatic: Most people only mocked, but Guo Jing of Wu and Ning Qu of Yangqu believed the omens and pooled money to help him.

sentences.zh: 勒亦感其恩，為之力耕。

translations.literal: Le also was moved by their kindness and for them ploughed with full strength.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le never forgot that kindness and repaid it by working the fields with all his might.

sentences.zh: 每聞鞞鐸之音，歸以告其母，母曰：「作勞耳鳴，非不祥也。」

translations.literal: Whenever he heard the sound of drum and bell from harnesses, he returned home to tell his mother; his mother said, "It is labour making the ears ring—it is not inauspicious."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he heard the jangle of harness bells, he would run home to tell his mother; she would say, "That is only your ears ringing from hard work—not a bad omen."

sentences.zh: 太安中，幷州饑亂，勒與諸小胡亡散，乃自雁門還依甯驅。

translations.literal: In the Tai'an years, Bingzhou was afflicted by famine and turmoil; Le with various young Hu scattered in flight, then from Yanmen returned to depend on Ning Qu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tai'an era famine and chaos tore through Bingzhou; Shi Le, scattered with other young Hu, doubled back from Yanmen to take shelter with Ning Qu.

sentences.zh: 北澤都尉劉監欲縛賣之，驅匿之，獲免。

translations.literal: The commander of Beize, Liu Jian, wished to bind and sell him; Qu hid him, and he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The northern-marsh commandant Liu Jian tried to seize and sell him as a slave, but Ning Qu hid him until the danger passed.

sentences.zh: 勒於是潛詣納降都尉李川，路逢郭敬，泣拜言-{飢}-寒。

translations.literal: Thereupon Le secretly went to the surrender-receiving commandant Li Chuan; on the road he met Guo Jing, wept and bowed, speaking of hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le then slipped away to present himself to Li Chuan, the officer who received surrendering bands—and on the way met Guo Jing, threw himself down weeping, and poured out how hungry and cold he was.

sentences.zh: 敬對之流涕，以帶貨鬻食之，-{幷}-給以衣服。

translations.literal: Jing, confronting him, shed tears; with goods from his belt he pawned them to buy food for him, and also gave him clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jing wept at the sight of him, pawned part of his own belt to buy food, and gave Shi Le clothes besides.

sentences.zh: 勒謂敬曰：「今者大餓，不可守窮。

translations.literal: Le said to Jing, "At present there is great famine; one cannot guard poverty."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le told him, "People are starving to death—we cannot simply cling to poverty and do nothing."

sentences.zh: 諸胡-{飢}-甚，宜誘將冀州就穀，因執賣之，可以兩濟。

translations.literal: The various Hu are extremely hungry; it is fitting to entice them to lead them to Jizhou to obtain grain, and there seize and sell them—thus both sides can be aided."
translations.idiomatic: The other Hu are starving. Lure them into Jizhou for grain, then round them up and sell them—you feed your people and turn a profit at the same time."

sentences.zh: 」敬深然之。

translations.literal: Jing deeply approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jing agreed that the plan made sense.

sentences.zh: 會建威將軍閻粹說幷州刺史、東嬴公騰執諸胡於山東賣充軍實，騰使將軍郭陽、張隆虜羣胡將詣冀州，兩胡一枷。

translations.literal: It happened that the general who built awe, Yan Cui, persuaded the inspector of Bingzhou, the Duke of Eastern Ying, Teng, to seize the various Hu east of the mountains to sell them and replenish military supplies; Teng ordered the generals Guo Yang and Zhang Long to capture throngs of Hu and convey them toward Jizhou, two Hu per cangue.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Yan Cui, the general who built awe, talked the Bingzhou inspector Sima Teng, the Duke of Eastern Ying, into rounding up Hu east of the Taihang and selling them for war funds. Teng had Generals Guo Yang and Zhang Long shackle the captives two to a yoke and march them toward Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 勒時年二十餘，亦在其中，數為隆所驅辱。

translations.literal: Le at the time was more than twenty years of age and was also among them; several times he was driven and insulted by Long.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le, now in his twenties, was among them and suffered repeated abuse at Zhang Long's hands.

sentences.zh: 敬先以勒屬郭陽及兄子時，陽，敬族兄也，是以陽、時每為解請，道路-{飢}-病，賴陽、時而濟。

translations.literal: Jing earlier had entrusted Le to Guo Yang and Yang's nephew Shi; Yang was Jing's clansman, and therefore Yang and Shi always pleaded on his behalf; on the road, hunger and illness—he survived relying on Yang and Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jing had earlier placed Shi Le under Guo Yang and Yang's nephew Shi; because Yang was a kinsman of Jing's, the two repeatedly interceded for him so that hunger and sickness on the march did not kill him.

sentences.zh: 旣而賣與茌平人師懽為奴。

translations.literal: Later he was sold to the man from Chiping, Shi Huan, as a slave.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually he was sold into slavery to Shi Huan of Chiping.

sentences.zh: 有一老父謂勒曰：「君魚龍髮際上四道已成，當貴為人主。

translations.literal: An old man said to Le, "On your hairline above the temples four lines of the fish-dragon pattern are already complete; you will honourably become a lord of men.
translations.idiomatic: An old stranger told him, "The 'fish-dragon' lines at your temples are complete—you are fated to rule men as a sovereign."

sentences.zh: 甲戌之歲，王彭祖可圖。

translations.literal: In the year jiaxu, Wang Pengzu can be plotted against."
translations.idiomatic: In the jiaxu year you may move against Wang Pengzu."

sentences.zh: 」勒曰：「若如公言，弗敢忘德。

translations.literal: Le said, "If it is as the elder said, I dare not forget your virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le replied, "If what you say comes true, I will not forget this kindness."

sentences.zh: 」忽然不見。

translations.literal: Suddenly he was no longer visible.
translations.idiomatic: Then the old man vanished as suddenly as he had appeared.

sentences.zh: 每耕作於野，常聞鼓角之聲。

translations.literal: Whenever he ploughed in the fields, he constantly heard drum and horn sounds.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he worked the fields he kept hearing drums and horns, though no army was there.

sentences.zh: 勒以告諸奴，諸奴亦聞之，因曰：「吾幼來在家恆聞如是。

translations.literal: Le reported it to the various slaves; the various slaves also heard it, and therefore said, "I since youth at home constantly have heard it thus."
translations.idiomatic: He told the other bondsmen; they heard it too, and said they had heard the same sounds at home since childhood.

sentences.zh: 」諸奴歸以告懽，懽亦奇其狀貌而免之。

translations.literal: The slaves returned and reported to Huan; Huan also thought his appearance strange and released him.
translations.idiomatic: They went home and told Shi Huan, who was struck by Shi Le's bearing and freed him from servitude.

sentences.zh: 懽家鄰於馬牧，與牧率魏郡汲桑往來，勒以能相馬自託於桑。

translations.literal: Huan's household neighboured the horse pasture; he had dealings with Ji Sang the pasture chief from Ji county in Wei commandery; Le, relying on ability to judge horses, attached himself to Sang.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Huan's farm bordered the imperial horse pasture, where he knew Ji Sang, the herders' chief from Ji in Wei; Shi Le, boasting a gift for judging horses, made himself useful to Ji Sang.

sentences.zh: 嘗傭於武安臨水，為遊軍所囚。

translations.literal: Once hired out at Linshui in Wu'an, he was imprisoned by a roaming patrol.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while hired out at Linshui in Wu'an, he was seized by a roving patrol.

sentences.zh: 會有羣鹿旁過，軍人競逐之，勒乃獲免。

translations.literal: It happened that a herd of deer passed nearby; the soldiers vied to pursue them, and Le thereby obtained release.
translations.idiomatic: A herd of deer happened by; the soldiers rushed off in pursuit, and Shi Le used the confusion to escape.

sentences.zh: 俄而又見一父老，謂勒曰：「向羣鹿者我也，君應為中州主，故相救爾。

translations.literal: Shortly he again saw an old man, who said to Le, "Those deer a moment ago were me; you ought to become lord of the Central Plain; therefore I saved you."
translations.idiomatic: Soon another greybeard appeared and said, "Those deer were myself in disguise—you are meant to master the Central Plain, which is why I rescued you."

sentences.zh: 」勒拜而受命。

translations.literal: Le bowed and accepted the charge.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le bowed and accepted the charge.

sentences.zh: 遂招集王陽、夔安、支雄、冀保、吳豫、劉膺、桃豹、逯明等八騎為羣盜。

translations.literal: Thereupon he gathered Wang Yang, Kui An, Zhi Xiong, Ji Bao, Wu Yu, Liu Ying, Tao Bao, Lu Ming and others, eight riders as a band of robbers.
translations.idiomatic: He then gathered Wang Yang, Kui An, Zhi Xiong, Ji Bao, Wu Yu, Liu Ying, Tao Bao, Lu Ming, and seven others—eight horsemen who turned bandit.

sentences.zh: 後郭敖、劉徵、劉寶、張曀僕、呼延莫、郭黑略、張越、孔豚、趙鹿、支屈六等又赴之，號為十八騎。

translations.literal: Later Guo Ao, Liu Zheng, Liu Bao, Zhang Yipu, Huyan Mo, Guo Heilue, Zhang Yue, Kong Tun, Zhao Lu, Zhi Quliu and others also joined; they were called the Eighteen Riders.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ao, Liu Zheng, Liu Bao, Zhang Yipu, Huyan Mo, Guo Heilue, Zhang Yue, Kong Tun, Zhao Lu, Zhi Quliu, and others soon joined them, and the band was known as the Eighteen Riders.

sentences.zh: 復東如赤龍、騄驥諸苑中，乘苑馬遠掠繒寶，以賂汲桑。

translations.literal: Again east to various parks such as Chilong and Luji, mounting park horses they raided far for silks and treasures to bribe Ji Sang.
translations.idiomatic: They rode east into imperial studs such as Chilong and Luji, stole mounts and silks on long raids, and used the loot to buy Ji Sang's favour.

sentences.zh: 及成都王穎敗乘輿-{于}-蕩陰，逼帝如鄴宮，王浚以穎陵辱天子，使鮮卑擊之，穎懼，挾惠帝南奔洛陽。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Chengdu, Ying, defeated the imperial carriage at Dangyin and forced the emperor toward the Ye palace, Wang Jun, because Ying had humiliated the Son of Heaven, sent Xianbei to strike him; Ying feared and, clasping Emperor Hui, fled south to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Sima Ying, Prince of Chengdu, routed the imperial escort at Dangyin and marched Emperor Hui toward Ye, Wang Jun—outraged at Ying's treatment of the sovereign—sent Xianbei against him. Ying broke and fled south to Luoyang with the emperor in tow.

sentences.zh: 帝復為張方所逼，遷-{于}-長安。

translations.literal: The emperor again was compelled by Zhang Fang and moved to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fang then forced the court to abandon Luoyang and withdraw to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 關東所在兵起，皆以誅穎為名。

translations.literal: East of the Pass everywhere soldiers rose, all in the name of executing Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Across the eastern heartland every warlord raised arms, each claiming to punish Sima Ying.

sentences.zh: 河間王顒懼東師之盛，欲輯懷東復，乃奏議廢穎。

translations.literal: The Prince of Hejian, Yong, feared the strength of the eastern hosts and wished to conciliate the east to restore relations; therefore he memorialized debating deposing Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yong, Prince of Hejian, feared the eastern coalition and sought to appease it by sponsoring a memorial to depose Ying.

sentences.zh: 是歲，劉元海稱漢王-{于}-黎亭，穎故將陽平人公師籓等自稱將軍，起兵趙魏，衆至數萬。

translations.literal: That year Liu Yuanhai declared himself King of Han at Liting; Ying's former general Gong Shifan and others from Yangping styled themselves generals, raised troops in Zhao and Wei, and their masses reached several tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Liu Yuan proclaimed himself Han king at Liting, while Gong Shifan of Yangping—once Ying's subordinate—and others declared themselves generals and mustered tens of thousands across Zhao and Wei.

sentences.zh: 勒與汲桑帥牧人乘苑馬數百騎以赴之。

translations.literal: Le together with Ji Sang led herdsmen riding several hundred park horses to join them.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le and Ji Sang led several hundred mounted herders on stolen stud horses to join the rising.

sentences.zh: 桑始命勒以石為姓，勒為名焉。

translations.literal: Sang first ordered Le to take Shi as surname and Le as name.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Sang was the one who told him to adopt Shi as his surname and Le as his personal name.

sentences.zh: 籓拜勒為前隊督，從攻平昌公模於鄴。

translations.literal: Fan appointed Le forward-column commander and followed to attack the Duke of Pingchang, Mo, at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Shifan named him front-column commander and took him along to strike Sima Mo, the Duke of Pingchang, at Ye.

sentences.zh: 模使將軍馮嵩逆戰，敗之。

translations.literal: Mo sent the general Feng Song to meet them in battle and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Mo sent General Feng Song to intercept them and broke their army.

sentences.zh: 籓濟自白馬而南，濮陽太守苟晞討籓斬之。

translations.literal: Fan crossed from Baima southward; the prefect of Puyang, Gou Xi, attacked Fan and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Shifan crossed south from Baima, but Gou Xi, the prefect of Puyang, attacked his column and struck off his head.

sentences.zh: 勒與桑亡潛苑中，桑以勒為伏夜牙門，帥牧人劫掠郡縣繫囚，又招山澤亡命，多附勒，勒率以應之。

translations.literal: Le with Sang fled hiding in the parks; Sang made Le night-raid gate commander of ambush, leading herdsmen to pillage counties and seize prisoners; also he summoned renegades from mountains and marshes, many of whom attached to Le; Le led them to respond.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le fled with Ji Sang into the horse parks. Ji Sang made him warden of the night-raid gate while herders raided counties, broke jails, and drew in outlaws from hill and marsh; many rallied to Shi Le, and he brought them into Ji Sang's camp.

sentences.zh: 桑乃自號大將軍，稱為成都王穎誅東海王越、東嬴公騰為名。

translations.literal: Thereupon Sang styled himself grand general, declaring in the name of the Prince of Chengdu Ying the execution of Prince Donghai Yue and the Duke of Eastern Ying Teng.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Sang then proclaimed himself grand general, raising the banner of avenging Sima Ying by punishing Sima Yue, Prince of Donghai, and Sima Teng, Duke of Eastern Ying.

sentences.zh: 桑以勒為前驅，屢有戰功，署為掃虜將軍、忠明亭侯。

translations.literal: Sang made Le vanguard; repeatedly there were martial achievements; posted him General Who Sweeps the Barbarians, marquis of Zhongming precinct.
translations.idiomatic: He kept Shi Le in the van; after a string of victories he brevetted him General Who Sweeps the Caitiffs and Marquis of Zhongming hamlet.

sentences.zh: 桑進軍攻鄴，以勒為前鋒都督，大敗騰將馮嵩，因長驅入鄴，遂害騰，殺萬餘人，掠婦女珍寶而去。

translations.literal: Sang advanced the army to attack Ye, made Le vanguard commander-in-chief, greatly defeated Teng's general Feng Song, then drove straight into Ye, thereupon slew Teng, killed more than ten thousand people, plundered women and treasures and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Sang drove on Ye with Shi Le as forward commander, shattered Sima Teng's general Feng Song, swept into the city, killed Teng himself, slaughtered over ten thousand, and withdrew laden with women and loot.

sentences.zh: 濟自延津，南擊兗州，越大懼，使苟晞、王贊等討之。

translations.literal: They crossed from Yanjin southward and struck Yanzhou; Yue greatly feared and sent Gou Xi, Wang Zan and others to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: From Yanjin they swung south into Yanzhou. Sima Yue, alarmed, sent Gou Xi, Wang Zan, and others against them.

sentences.zh: 桑、勒攻幽州刺史石尟於樂陵，尟死之。

translations.literal: Sang and Le attacked the Inspector of Youzhou Shi Xian at Leling; Xian died in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Sang and Shi Le stormed Leling, where Youzhou inspector Shi Xian fell in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 乞活田禋帥衆五萬救尟，勒逆戰，敗禋，與晞等相持-{于}-平原、陽平間數月，大小三十餘戰，互有勝負。

translations.literal: The Qi-huo leader Tian Yin led fifty thousand to rescue Xian; Le met them in battle, defeated Yin, and with Xi and others stood off for several months between Pingyuan and Yangping, thirty-odd great and small battles, each side having victories and defeats.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yin of the Qihuo bands brought fifty thousand men to relieve Shi Xian; Shi Le met him in the field and broke his force, then sparred with Gou Xi for months between Pingyuan and Yangping in more than thirty clashes that swayed back and forth.

sentences.zh: 越懼，次於官渡，為晞聲援。

translations.literal: Yue feared and halted at Guandu to sound support for Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue halted at Guandu to back Gou Xi with his presence.

sentences.zh: 桑、勒為晞所敗，死者萬餘人，乃收餘衆，將奔劉元海。

translations.literal: Sang and Le were defeated by Xi; more than ten thousand died; then they gathered the remainder and intended to flee to Liu Yuanhai.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Sang and Shi Le finally lost to Gou Xi, leaving ten thousand dead; they scraped together the survivors and prepared to bolt to Liu Yuan.

sentences.zh: 冀州刺史丁紹要之-{于}-赤橋，又大敗之。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Jizhou Ding Shao intercepted them at Chiqiao and again greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhou inspector Ding Shao ambushed them at Chiqiao and shattered them again.

sentences.zh: 桑奔馬牧，勒奔樂平。

translations.literal: Sang fled to the horse pasture; Le fled to Leping.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Sang fled toward the royal pastures while Shi Le raced for Leping.

sentences.zh: 王師斬桑-{于}-平原。

translations.literal: Imperial forces beheaded Sang at Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops caught Ji Sang on the plain and executed him.

sentences.zh: 時胡部大張㔨督、馮莫突等擁衆數千，壁-{于}-上黨，勒往從之，深為所昵，因說㔨督曰：「劉單-{于}-舉兵誅晉，部大距而不從，豈能獨立乎？

translations.literal: At the time the Hu chieftains Zhang Beidu, Feng Motuo and others had several thousand followers, fortifying themselves at Shangdang; Le went to join them, was deeply liked, and therefore persuaded Beidu, saying, "The Liu Chanyu has raised troops to punish Jin; a buluo dad refuses to follow—can he stand alone?"
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Hu headmen such as Zhang Beidu and Feng Motuo held several thousand warriors in a fort on Shangdang. Shi Le joined them, won their trust, and urged Zhang Beidu, "Liu Yuan, the Chanyu, has risen to overthrow the Jin; if a tribal chief hangs back, can he stand alone?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「不能。

translations.literal: (Beidu) said, "Cannot."
translations.idiomatic: "No," the chief admitted.

sentences.zh: 」勒曰：「如其不能者，兵馬當有所屬。

translations.literal: Le said, "If it is that you cannot, the soldiers and horses ought to have something they belong to."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le pressed him: "If not, then every horse and spear must answer to someone else."

sentences.zh: 今部落皆已被單-{于}-賞募，往往聚議欲叛部大而歸單-{于}-矣，宜早為之計。

translations.literal: "Now the tribes have all already been rewarded and recruited by the Chanyu; often they gather in council intending to rebel against the buluo dads and return to the Chanyu; you should plan early."
translations.idiomatic: "The camps have already taken Liu Yuan's gold and orders; men whisper of turning on their headmen to march for the Chanyu. Decide now, before they decide for you."

sentences.zh: 」㔨督等素無智略，懼部衆之貳己也，乃潛隨勒單騎歸元海。

translations.literal: Beidu and others by nature lacked stratagem, feared the tribe's hearts would turn from them, and covertly followed Le alone on horseback to return to Yuanhai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Beidu had little guile and feared losing his followers, so he stole away with Shi Le on a single horse to surrender to Liu Yuan.

sentences.zh: 元海署㔨督親漢王，莫突為都督部大，以勒為輔漢將軍、平晉王以統之。

translations.literal: Yuanhai appointed Beidu Prince Who Relies on Han, Motuo as commander buluo dad, and Le as General Who Supports Han and Prince Who Pacifies Jin to command them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan ennobled Zhang Beidu as prince of the Han-leaning house, named Feng Motuo chief of the tribal command, and made Shi Le General Who Supports Han and Prince Who Pacifies Jin to lead the whole body.

sentences.zh: 勒於是命㔨督為兄，賜姓石氏，名之曰會，言其遇己也。

translations.literal: Le thereupon ordered Beidu to be elder brother, bestowed surname Shi, named him Hui, meaning that he had met himself.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le treated Zhang Beidu as an elder brother, gave him the surname Shi, and renamed him Hui—"one who met me"—to mark their encounter.

sentences.zh: 烏丸張伏利度亦有衆二千，壁-{于}-樂平，元海屢招而不能致。

translations.literal: The Wuhuan Zhang Folidu also had two thousand followers, fortifying at Leping; Yuanhai repeatedly summoned but could not bring him in.
translations.idiomatic: The Wuhuan leader Zhang Folidu also walled up two thousand fighters at Leping; Liu Yuan courted him for years without success.

sentences.zh: 勒偽獲罪-{于}-元海，因奔伏利度。

translations.literal: Le feigned having incurred guilt toward Yuanhai and thereby fled to Folidu.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le pretended to have offended Liu Yuan and fled to Zhang Folidu for refuge.

sentences.zh: 伏利度大悅，結為兄弟，使勒率諸胡寇掠，所向無前，諸胡畏服。

translations.literal: Folidu greatly rejoiced, swore brotherhood with him, made Le lead the various Hu in raiding; wherever aimed none stood in front; the various Hu feared and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Folidu welcomed him eagerly, swore brotherhood, and put him at the head of Hu raiding parties that swept all before them until every band feared and obeyed him.

sentences.zh: 勒知衆心之附己也，乃因會執伏利度，告諸胡曰：「今起大事，我與伏利度孰堪為主？

translations.literal: Le knew the hearts of the masses leaned to himself; then at a gathering he seized Folidu and told the various Hu, "Now we raise a great affair—between me and Folidu, who is fit to be lord?"
translations.idiomatic: Once Shi Le saw the men were his, he seized Zhang Folidu at a feast and demanded of the Hu, "We mean to shake the realm—which of us two should lead?"

sentences.zh: 」諸胡咸以推勒。

translations.literal: The various Hu all pushed for Le.
translations.idiomatic: Every voice in the hall cried for Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 勒於是釋伏利度，率其部衆歸元海。

translations.literal: Le thereupon released Folidu and led his tribal followers to return to Yuanhai.
translations.idiomatic: He released Zhang Folidu, then marched the entire command back to Liu Yuan.

sentences.zh: 元海加勒督山東征討諸軍事，以伏利度衆配之。

translations.literal: Yuanhai added to Le supervisor of military affairs for the east-of-the-mountains campaigns, attaching Folidu's host to him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan added him as overseer of all eastern campaigns beyond the passes and folded Zhang Folidu's troops into his command.

sentences.zh: 元海使劉聰攻壺關，命勒率所統七千為前鋒都督。

translations.literal: Yuanhai sent Liu Cong to attack Huguan, ordering Le to lead his command of seven thousand as vanguard commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yuan sent Liu Cong against Huguan, he told Shi Le to take his seven thousand veterans as forward commander.

sentences.zh: 劉琨遣護軍黃秀等救壺關，勒敗秀於白田，秀死之，勒遂陷壺關。

translations.literal: Liu Kun sent the protector Huang Xiu and others to relieve Huguan; Le defeated Xiu at Baitian; Xiu died; thereupon Le took Huguan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun's rescuer Huang Xiu tried to relieve the city, but Shi Le cut him down at Baitian and stormed Huguan.

sentences.zh: 元海命勒與劉零、閻羆等七將率衆三萬寇魏郡、頓丘諸壘壁，多陷之，假壘主將軍、都尉，簡強壯五萬為軍士，老弱安堵如故，軍無私掠，百姓懷之。

translations.literal: Yuanhai ordered Le together with Liu Ling, Yan Pi and seven other generals to lead thirty thousand to raid Wei commandery and Dunqiu stockades; many were taken; he appointed the stockade masters generals and commandants, selected fifty thousand strong adult males as soldiers, the old and weak settled in peace as before, the army made no private plunder; the common people cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan next sent Shi Le with Liu Ling, Yan Pi, and seven other generals at the head of thirty thousand to tear through the fort lines of Wei and Dunqiu. Stockade chiefs who yielded were brevetted generals or commandants; fifty thousand able men were drafted, while elders and children were left unmolested. There was no private looting, and the people began to bless his name.

sentences.zh: 及元海僭號，遣使授勒持節、平東大將軍，校尉、都督、王如故。

translations.literal: When Yuanhai presumptuously assumed the imperial title, he sent envoys to invest Le with staff of authority, grand general who pacifies the east, with colonel-in-chief, commander-in-chief, and prince as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yuan declared himself emperor, he dispatched envoys to confirm Shi Le as grand general who pacifies the east with full insignia, keeping his old ranks of colonel, commander, and prince.

sentences.zh: 勒幷軍寇鄴，鄴潰，和郁奔-{于}-衛國。

translations.literal: Le combined forces and raided Ye; Ye collapsed; He Yu fled to Weiguo.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le united his columns, stormed Ye, and broke the defenses; He Yu, the governor, bolted for Weiguo.

sentences.zh: 執魏郡太守王粹-{于}-三臺。

translations.literal: Seized Wei commandery prefect Wang Cui at Santai.
translations.idiomatic: On Santai terrace he captured Wei prefect Wang Cui.

sentences.zh: 進攻趙郡，害冀州西部都尉馮沖。

translations.literal: Advanced to attack Zhao commandery and killed the western-department commandant of Jizhou, Feng Chong.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed into Zhao commandery and killed Feng Chong, Jizhou's western-department commandant.

sentences.zh: 攻乞活赦亭、田禋-{于}-中丘，皆殺之。

translations.literal: Attacked the Qihuo at Sheting and Tian Yin at Zhongqiu, and killed them both.
translations.idiomatic: He struck the Qihuo strongholds of Sheting and Tian Yin at Zhongqiu and put both leaders to the sword.

sentences.zh: 元海授勒安東大將軍、開府，置左右長史、司馬、從事中郎。

translations.literal: Yuanhai invested Le as grand general of the east, opening office, establishing left and right senior clerks, marshals, and adjutants.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan then promoted him to grand general of the east with authority to open a staff, appointing senior clerks, marshals, and adjutants on left and right.

sentences.zh: 進軍攻鉅鹿、常山，害二郡守將。

translations.literal: Advanced to attack Julu and Changshan and killed the defending prefects of the two commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: His columns overran Julu and Changshan and killed both garrison commanders.

sentences.zh: 陷冀州郡縣堡壁百餘，衆至十餘萬，其衣冠人物集為君子營。

translations.literal: He took more than a hundred stockades of Jizhou commanderies and counties; his masses reached more than one hundred thousand; gentry and notables were gathered into a Gentleman's Camp.
translations.idiomatic: He reduced more than a hundred walled settlements across Jizhou until his host topped a hundred thousand, and he grouped scholars and notables into an elite "gentlemen's camp."

sentences.zh: 乃引張賓為謀主，始署軍功曹，以刁膺、張敬為股肱，夔安、孔萇為爪牙，支雄、呼延莫、王陽、桃豹、逯明、吳豫等為將率。

translations.literal: Thereupon he brought in Zhang Bin as chief planner; first he established a bureau of military merit, with Diao Ying and Zhang Jing as arms, Kui An and Kong Chang as claws, Zhi Xiong, Huyan Mo, Wang Yang, Tao Bao, Lu Ming, Wu Yu and others as commanders.
translations.idiomatic: He then took Zhang Bin as chief strategist, set up a bureau of military merit, paired Diao Ying and Zhang Jing as his principal lieutenants, Kui An and Kong Chang as his strong right hand, and named Zhi Xiong, Huyan Mo, Wang Yang, Tao Bao, Lu Ming, Wu Yu, and others field commanders.

sentences.zh: 使其將張斯率騎詣幷州山北諸郡縣，說諸胡羯，曉以安危。

translations.literal: He made his general Zhang Si lead cavalry to the commanderies north of the mountains in Bingzhou, persuading the various Hu and Jie, clarifying safety and danger.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered General Zhang Si to ride north of Taihang through the Bingzhou counties to preach doom or survival to every Hu and Jie band.

sentences.zh: 諸胡懼勒威名，多有附者。

translations.literal: The various Hu feared Le's martial name; many had parties who attached.
translations.idiomatic: The northern tribes quailed at Shi Le's reputation and flocked to his banner.

sentences.zh: 進軍常山，分遣諸將攻中山、博陵、高陽諸縣，降之者數萬人。

translations.literal: Advanced into Changshan, separately dispatching generals to attack Zhongshan, Boling, Gaoyang and other counties; those who submitted numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced on Changshan while detachments seized Zhongshan, Boling, Gaoyang, and other counties, adding tens of thousands of surrendered fighters.

sentences.zh: 王浚使其將祁弘帥鮮卑段務塵等十餘萬騎討勒，大敗勒-{于}-飛龍山，死者萬餘。

translations.literal: Wang Jun sent his general Qi Hong to lead Xianbei Duan Wuchen and more than one hundred thousand cavalry to campaign against Le, greatly defeated Le at Feilong Mountain; more than ten thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun answered by sending Qi Hong with Duan Wuchen's Xianbei—well over a hundred thousand horsemen—who crushed Shi Le on Feilong Mountain and left more than ten thousand dead.

sentences.zh: 勒退屯黎陽，分命諸將攻諸未下及叛者，降三十餘壁，置守宰以撫之。

translations.literal: Le withdrew to garrison Liyang, separately ordering generals to attack those not yet taken and those who rebelled, submitting more than thirty stockades; he placed guards and magistrates to soothe them.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le pulled back to Liyang, sent columns against holdouts and deserters, brought thirty-odd forts to heel, and installed magistrates to calm the countryside.

sentences.zh: 進寇信都，害冀州刺史王斌。

translations.literal: Advanced to raid Xindu and killed the inspector of Jizhou, Wang Bin.
translations.idiomatic: He then struck Xindu, killed Jizhou inspector Wang Bin, and tightened his grip on the province.

sentences.zh: 於是車騎將軍王堪、北中郎將裴憲自洛陽率衆討勒，勒燒營幷糧，迴軍距之，次-{于}-黃牛壘。

translations.literal: Thereupon the chariot-and-horse general Wang Kan and the north-centre general Pei Xian from Luoyang led masses to campaign against Le; Le burned camp and grain together, turned the army to oppose them, and halted at Huangniu Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kan, chariot-and-horse general, and Pei Xian, north-centre general, marched east from Luoyang; Shi Le burned his own camp and stores, wheeled about, and drew them up at Huangniu Stockade.

sentences.zh: 魏郡太守劉矩以郡附-{于}-勒，勒使矩統其壘衆為中軍左翼。

translations.literal: Wei commandery prefect Liu Ju attached his commandery to Le; Le made Ju command his stockade masses as middle army left wing.
translations.idiomatic: Wei prefect Liu Ju defected with his entire command, and Shi Le folded his militia into the middle army's left wing under Liu Ju's command.

sentences.zh: 勒至黎陽，裴憲棄其軍奔-{于}-淮南，王堪退堡倉垣。

translations.literal: Le reached Liyang; Pei Xian abandoned his army and fled to Huainan; Wang Kan withdrew to fortify Cangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Le closed on Liyang, Pei Xian threw away his army and ran for Huainan, while Wang Kan shrank behind the walls of Cangyuan.

sentences.zh: 元海授勒鎮東大將軍，封汲郡公，持節、都督、王如故。

translations.literal: Yuanhai invested Le as grand general who guards the east, enfeoffed him duke of Ji commandery, with staff of authority, commander-in-chief, and prince as before.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan then named him grand general who guards the east and duke of Ji, again with staff, command, and princely rank.

sentences.zh: 勒固讓公不受。

translations.literal: Le firmly declined the duke and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le repeatedly refused the ducal patent and would not take the seal.

sentences.zh: 與閻羆攻䐗者圈、苑市二壘，陷之，羆中流矢死，勒幷統其衆，潛自石橋濟河，攻陷白馬，坑男女三千餘口。

translations.literal: Together with Yan Pi he attacked the two stockades at Zhuzhequan and Yuan Market, overran them, and Pi was struck by a stray arrow and died; Le then absorbed their troops, slipped across the river by the stone bridge, stormed Baima, and buried alive more than three thousand captives, men and women.
translations.idiomatic: With Yan Pi he stormed the twin forts of Zhuzhequan and Yuan Market; Pi fell to a stray shaft, and Shi Le rolled their bands into his own command, forded secretly at the stone bridge, seized Baima, and slaughtered three thousand townspeople in a burial pit.

sentences.zh: 東襲鄄城，害兗州刺史袁孚。

translations.literal: He struck east at Juancheng and killed Yuan Fu, the inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He swept east against Juancheng and cut down Yanzhou inspector Yuan Fu.

sentences.zh: 因攻倉垣，陷之，遂害堪。

translations.literal: He then stormed Cangyuan, took it, and killed Wang Kan.
translations.idiomatic: Next he broke Cangyuan, put the city to the torch, and executed Wang Kan.

sentences.zh: 渡河攻廣宗、清河、平原、陽平諸縣，降勒者九萬餘口。

translations.literal: Crossing the river he attacked Guangzong, Qinghe, Pingyuan, Yangping, and other counties; those who submitted to Le numbered more than ninety thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: After the crossing his columns rolled through Guangzong, Qinghe, Pingyuan, and Yangping until more than ninety thousand people capitulated to him.

sentences.zh: 復南濟河，滎陽太守裴純奔-{于}-建業。

translations.literal: Again he crossed south of the river; the prefect of Xingyang, Pei Chun, fled to Jianye -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: He recrossed the Great River; Xingyang prefect Pei Chun abandoned his post and ran for the Eastern Jin capital at Jianye -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 時劉聰攻河內，勒率騎會之，攻冠軍將軍梁巨-{于}-武德，懷帝遣兵救之。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Cong was besieging Henei; Le led cavalry to join him and attacked the champion general Liang Ju at Wude; Emperor Huai dispatched troops to relieve Ju -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: While Liu Cong pressed Henei, Shi Le rode to his aid and pinned Champion General Liang Ju at Wude, prompting Emperor Huai to send a relief column -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 勒留諸將守武德，與王桑逆巨於長陵。

translations.literal: Le left generals to hold Wude and with Wang Sang met Ju at Changling.
translations.idiomatic: He posted a rearguard at Wude, then joined Wang Sang to intercept Liang Ju near Changling.

sentences.zh: 巨請降，勒弗許，巨逾城而遁，軍人執之。

translations.literal: Ju asked to surrender; Le would not permit it; Ju climbed over the wall and fled, but soldiers seized him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Ju offered capitulation; Shi Le refused, so Ju tried to scale the wall at night only to be dragged down by the pickets.

sentences.zh: 勒馳如武德，坑降卒萬餘，數梁巨罪而害之。

translations.literal: Le galloped to Wude, buried alive more than ten thousand surrendered soldiers, enumerated Liang Ju's crimes, and put him to death.
translations.idiomatic: He raced back to Wude, entombed ten thousand prisoners in a pit, recited Liang Ju's crimes, and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 王師退還，河北諸堡壁大震，皆請降送任-{于}-勒。

translations.literal: Imperial forces withdrew; stockades north of the Yellow River trembled and all begged to submit, sending hostages to Le -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: When the government armies pulled back, every fortified village along the Hebei corridor sued for terms and sent hostages to Shi Le -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 及元海死，劉聰授勒征東大將軍、幷州刺史、汲郡公，持節、開府、都督、校尉、王如故。

translations.literal: When Yuanhai died, Liu Cong appointed Le grand general who campaigns east, inspector of Bingzhou, duke of Ji commandery, with staff, opened office, commander-in-chief, colonel-in-chief, and prince as before.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Yuan's death Liu Cong confirmed Shi Le as grand general of the eastern campaigns, Bingzhou inspector, and duke of Ji, while renewing his staff, opened office, command, colonelcy, and princely title.

sentences.zh: 勒固辭將軍，乃止。

translations.literal: Le firmly declined the generalship, and therefore it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le repeatedly refused the general's commission until Liu Cong let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 劉粲率衆四萬寇洛陽，勒留輜重-{于}-重門，率騎二萬會粲于大陽，大敗王師於澠池，遂至洛川。

translations.literal: Liu Can led forty thousand to raid Luoyang; Le left baggage at Chongmen, led twenty thousand horse to join Can at Dayang, shattered the imperial army at Mianchi, and reached the Luo plain -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can marched forty thousand on Luoyang; Shi Le parked his train at Chongmen, rode twenty thousand to link with Can at Dayang, shattered the court army at Mianchi, and swept onto the Luo river plain -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 粲出轘轅，勒出成皋關，圍陳留太守王贊於倉垣，為贊所敗，退屯文石津。

translations.literal: Can exited Huanyuan; Le exited Chenggao Pass and besieged Wang Zan, prefect of Chenliu, at Cangyuan; he was defeated by Zan and withdrew to garrison Wenshi Ford.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can took the Huanyuan road while Shi Le burst through Chenggao and pinned Chenliu prefect Wang Zan at Cangyuan—only to lose to Wang Zan and fall back on Wenshi Ford.

sentences.zh: 將北攻王浚，會浚將王甲始率遼西鮮卑萬餘騎敗趙固-{于}-津北，勒乃燒船棄營，引軍向柏門，迎重門輜重，至-{于}-石門，濟河，攻襄城太守崔曠於繁昌，害之。

translations.literal: He intended to strike north at Wang Jun, but Jun's officer Wang Jiashi led more than ten thousand Liaoxi Xianbei to defeat Zhao Gu north of the ford; Le therefore burned ships, abandoned camp, led the army toward Baimen, met the Chongmen baggage, reached Shimen, crossed the river, attacked Xiangcheng prefect Cui Kuang at Fanchang, and killed him -{yu}- -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to march on Wang Jun until Jun's man Wang Jiashi shattered Zhao Gu north of the crossing with ten thousand Liaoxi Xianbei; Shi Le scuttled his boats, abandoned camp, doubled back through Baimen for his supply train at Shimen, crossed the river, stormed Fanchang, and killed Xiangcheng prefect Cui Kuang -{yu}- -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 先是，雍州流人王如、侯脫、嚴嶷等起兵江淮間，聞勒之來也，懼，遣衆一萬屯襄城以距，勒擊敗之，盡俘其衆。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wang Ru, Hou Tuo, Yan Yi and other displaced people from Yongzhou had risen between the Yangzi and Huai; hearing of Le's approach they feared and sent ten thousand to garrison Xiangcheng to resist; Le defeated them and took all captive.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Yongzhou exiles Wang Ru, Hou Tuo, and Yan Yi had rebelled between the Yangzi and Huai; dreading Shi Le's advance they stacked ten thousand men at Xiangcheng, yet he broke the line and bagged every survivor.

sentences.zh: 勒至南陽，屯-{于}-宛北山。

translations.literal: Le reached Nanyang and encamped on the hills north of Wan -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed into Nanyang and camped on the ridges north of Wan city -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 如懼勒之攻襄也，使送珍寶車馬犒師，結為兄弟，勒納之。

translations.literal: Ru feared Le's attack on Xiang and sent treasures, chariots, and horses to reward the army, swearing brotherhood; Le accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ru, terrified that Xiangcheng would be next, sent gold, carriages, and mounts as a bribe and offered blood brotherhood; Shi Le took the gifts.

sentences.zh: 如與侯脫不平，說勒攻脫。

translations.literal: Ru was at odds with Hou Tuo and urged Le to attack Tuo.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ru, feuding with Hou Tuo, talked Shi Le into moving against him.

sentences.zh: 勒夜令三軍雞鳴而駕，晨壓宛門，攻之，旬有二日而克。

translations.literal: Le ordered the three armies to harness at cockcrow; at dawn he pressed the gates of Wan and stormed the city, taking it in twelve days.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered every regiment saddled at the cock's crow, rolled up to Wan's gates at dawn, and cracked the walls after a twelve-day siege.

sentences.zh: 嚴嶷率衆救脫，至則無及，遂降-{于}-勒。

translations.literal: Yan Yi led troops to save Tuo, but arrived too late and therefore surrendered to Le -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yi marched to relieve Hou Tuo, arrived too late, and offered Shi Le his sword -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 勒斬脫，囚嶷送於平陽，盡幷其衆，軍勢彌盛。

translations.literal: Le beheaded Tuo, imprisoned Yi and sent him to Pingyang, annexed all their troops, and his military power grew still greater.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le beheaded Hou Tuo, shackled Yan Yi for shipment to Pingyang, swallowed their armies, and loomed larger than ever.

sentences.zh: 勒南寇襄陽，攻陷江西壘壁三十餘所，留刁膺守襄陽，躬帥精騎三萬還攻王如。

translations.literal: Le raided south against Xiangyang, took more than thirty stockades west of the river, left Diao Ying to hold Xiangyang, and personally led thirty thousand picked horse back to attack Wang Ru.
translations.idiomatic: He swept the Han River west bank, leaving thirty stockades in ashes, posted Diao Ying at Xiangyang, then wheeled north with thirty thousand veterans to crush Wang Ru.

sentences.zh: 憚如之盛，遂趣襄城。

translations.literal: He feared Ru's strength and therefore hurried to Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wary of Wang Ru's numbers, he pivoted toward Xiangcheng instead.

sentences.zh: 如知之，遣弟璃率騎二萬五千，詐言犒軍，實欲襲勒。

translations.literal: Ru learned of it and sent his younger brother Wang Li with twenty-five thousand horse, claiming to reward the army but intending to surprise Le.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ru learned the move and sent his brother Wang Li with twenty-five thousand riders under the pretense of bringing supplies—actually planning a dawn strike.

sentences.zh: 勒逆擊，滅之，復屯江西，蓋欲有雄據江漢之志也。

translations.literal: Le met them in battle, annihilated them, again encamped west of the river—intending to dominate the Yangzi and Han.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le met the column head-on, wiped it out, and returned to the west-bank camps with designs on ruling the middle Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 張賓以為不可，勸勒北還，弗從，以賓為參軍都尉，領記室，位次司馬，專居中總事。

translations.literal: Zhang Bin thought it unfeasible and urged Le to return north; he did not follow, instead appointing Bin adjutant-in-chief of the army and chief of the secretariat, ranking below the marshal, dwelling within headquarters to manage all affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin argued that the south was a trap and begged him to march north; Shi Le brushed the counsel aside, named Zhang Bin adjutant and chief clerk just under the marshal, and kept him at headquarters running day-to-day policy.

sentences.zh: 元帝慮勒南寇，使王導率衆討勒。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan, fearing Le's southern raid, sent Wang Dao with an army to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin prince at Jiankang, fearing a southern thrust, ordered Wang Dao east with an expeditionary host.

sentences.zh: 勒軍糧不接，死疫太半，納張賓之策，乃焚輜重，裹糧卷甲，渡沔，寇江夏，太守楊岠棄郡而走。

translations.literal: Le's army ran short of grain; death and plague carried off more than half; adopting Zhang Bin's plan he burned the baggage, wrapped rations and rolled armour, crossed the Mian, raided Jiangxia, and prefect Yang Ju abandoned the commandery and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Supplies failed and plague halved his ranks until Zhang Bin convinced him to torch the wagons, pack dry rations, ford the Mian, strike Jiangxia, and send prefect Yang Ju running.

sentences.zh: 北寇新蔡，害新蔡王確-{于}-南頓，朗陵公何襲、廣陵公陳軫、上黨太守羊綜、廣平太守邵肇等率衆降-{于}-勒。

translations.literal: He raided north to Xincai, killed Prince Xincai Que at Nandun, and Langling duke He Xi, Guangling duke Chen Zhen, Shangdang prefect Yang Zong, Guangping prefect Shao Zhao and others led their hosts to surrender to Le -{yu}- -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: He swung north into Xincai, killed Prince Xincai Sima Que at Nandun, and watched Langling duke He Xi, Guangling duke Chen Zhen, Shangdang prefect Yang Zong, Guangping prefect Shao Zhao, and others bring their divisions over to him -{yu}- -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 勒進陷許昌，害平東將軍王康。

translations.literal: Le advanced and took Xuchang, killing the general who pacifies the east, Wang Kang.
translations.idiomatic: His van seized Xuchang and put to the sword Wang Kang, the general who pacifies the east.

sentences.zh: 先是，東海王越率洛陽之衆二十餘萬討勒，越薨-{于}-軍，衆推太尉王衍為主，率衆東下，勒輕騎追及之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Prince Donghai Yue had led more than two hundred thousand from Luoyang to campaign against Le; Yue died in the army; the masses pushed Grand Commandant Wang Yan as leader and marched east; Le with light horse overtook them -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Sima Yue, Prince of Donghai, had marched two hundred thousand Luoyang troops against Shi Le, only to die in camp; the host chose Wang Yan as chief and trudged east until Shi Le's light cavalry ran them down -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 衍遣將軍錢端與勒戰，為勒所敗，端死之，衍軍大潰，勒分騎圍而射之，相登如山，無一免者。

translations.literal: Yan sent general Qian Duan to battle Le; he was defeated by Le; Duan died; Yan's army utterly collapsed; Le divided horse to surround and shoot them; they piled atop one another like a mountain; none escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan sent Qian Duan; Shi Le shattered the column, left Qian Duan dead, and ringed the fugitives with horse archers until corpses mounded like a hill—no one survived.

sentences.zh: 於是執衍及襄陽王範、任城王濟、西河王喜、梁王禧、齊王超、吏部尚書劉望、豫州刺名劉喬、太傅長史庾顗等，坐之-{于}-幕下，問以晉故。

translations.literal: Thereupon he seized Yan and Princes Fan of Xiangyang, Ji of Rencheng, Xi of Xihe, Xi of Liang, Chao of Qi, Minister of Personnel Liu Wang, the inspector of Yuzhou Liu Qiao, chief clerk of the grand tutor Yu Yi, and others, seated them beneath his tent curtain, and questioned them on Jin affairs -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: He then rounded up Wang Yan, Princes Fan, Ji, Xi, Xi, and Chao, Minister Liu Wang, Yuzhou inspector Liu Qiao, Grand Tutor chief clerk Yu Yi, and the rest, seated them under his command tent, and quizzed them on the western court -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 衍、濟等懼死，多自陳說，惟範神色儼然，意氣自若，顧呵之曰：「今日之事，何復紛紜！

translations.literal: Yan, Ji and others feared death and mostly made excuses; only Fan remained composed in bearing and spirit, turned and rebuked them, saying, "What is all this chatter on a day like today!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan and Sima Ji babbled excuses for their lives, but Prince Fan sat rigid, wheeled on the others, and snapped, "Why all this noise on the day we die!"

sentences.zh: 」勒甚奇之。

translations.literal: Le greatly marvelled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le was struck with admiration.

sentences.zh: 勒於是引諸王公卿士於外害之，死者甚衆。

translations.literal: Le thereupon led the various princes, dukes, ministers, and gentry outside and killed them; the dead were very many.
translations.idiomatic: He marched the royal hostages outside the camp and cut them down in droves.

sentences.zh: 勒重衍清辨，奇範神氣，不能加之兵刃，夜使人排牆填殺之。

translations.literal: Le esteemed Yan's lucid debate and marvelled at Fan's spirit and could not bring himself to use the blade on them; at night he had men push walls over and crush them to death.
translations.idiomatic: He respected Wang Yan's eloquence and Prince Fan's bearing too much for a public beheading, so he had his guards topple a wall on them in the dark.

sentences.zh: 左衛何倫、右衛李惲聞越薨，奉越妃裴氏及越世子毗出自洛陽。

translations.literal: Left Guard He Lun and Right Guard Li Yun heard that Yue had died; they escorted Yue's consort Lady Pei and Yue's heir Pi out from Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Left Guard He Lun and Right Guard Li Yun, hearing of Sima Yue's death, convoyed Lady Pei and heir Sima Pi out of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 勒逆毗於洧倉，軍復大潰，執毗及諸王公卿士，皆害之，死者甚衆。

translations.literal: Le met Pi at Weicang; the army again utterly collapsed; he seized Pi and the various princes, dukes, ministers, and gentry, all killed them; the dead were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le intercepted Sima Pi at Weicang, shattered the escort, seized the prince and every noble in the train, and slaughtered them wholesale.

sentences.zh: 因率精騎三萬，入自成皋關。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led thirty thousand picked horse and entered through Chenggao Pass himself.
translations.idiomatic: He then drove thirty thousand veterans through Chenggao Pass.

sentences.zh: 會劉曜、王彌寇洛陽，洛陽旣陷，勒歸功彌、曜，遂出轘轅，屯-{于}-許昌。

translations.literal: It happened that Liu Yao and Wang Mi raided Luoyang; after Luoyang had fallen, Le attributed merit to Mi and Yao, then exited Huanyuan and encamped at Xuchang -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yao and Wang Mi sacked Luoyang, Shi Le ceded the glory to them, doubled back through Huanyuan, and camped at Xuchang -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 劉聰署勒征東大將軍，勒固辭不受。

translations.literal: Liu Cong appointed Le grand general who campaigns east; Le firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong tried to renew his title as grand general of the eastern campaigns; Shi Le refused the patent outright.

sentences.zh: 先是，平陽人李洪有衆數千，壘-{于}-舞陽，苟晞假洪雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Earlier, a Pingyang man Li Hong had several thousand followers, fortifying at Wuyang; Gou Xi had provisionally appointed Hong inspector of Yongzhou -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Hong of Pingyang had walled up a few thousand followers at Wuyang while Gou Xi brevetted him Yongzhou inspector -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 勒進寇穀陽，害冠軍將軍王茲。

translations.literal: Le advanced to raid Guyang and killed the champion general Wang Ci.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le stormed Guyang and killed Champion General Wang Ci.

sentences.zh: 破王讚-{于}-陽夏，獲讚，以為從事中郎。

translations.literal: He broke Wang Zan at Yangxia, captured Zan, and appointed him adjutant -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: He smashed Wang Zan at Yangxia, took him alive, and named him an adjutant -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 襲破大將軍苟晞-{于}-蒙城，執晞，署為左司馬。

translations.literal: He surprised and broke Grand General Gou Xi at Mengcheng, seized Xi, and appointed him left marshal -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: He ambushed Grand General Gou Xi at Mengcheng, bagged him, and installed him as left marshal—on paper -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 劉聰授勒征東大將軍、幽州牧，固辭將軍不受。

translations.literal: Liu Cong appointed Le grand general who campaigns east and shepherd of Youzhou; he firmly declined the generalship and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong added Youzhou shepherd to the eastern generalship; Shi Le again declined the military half of the bundle.

sentences.zh: 先是，王彌納劉暾之說，將先誅勒，東王青州，使暾徵其將曹嶷於齊。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wang Mi had adopted Liu Tun's plan intending first to kill Le, then rule Qingzhou east; he sent Tun to summon his general Cao Yi from Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wang Mi, heeding Liu Tun, had plotted to murder Shi Le before carving out Qingzhou and had Liu Tun recall general Cao Yi from Qi.

sentences.zh: 勒遊騎獲暾，得彌所與嶷書，勒殺之，密有圖彌之計矣。

translations.literal: Le's roaming horse captured Tun, obtaining Mi's letter to Yi; Le killed him and secretly harboured a plan to eliminate Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le's patrols seized Liu Tun with Wang Mi's letter to Cao Yi; Shi Le executed Tun and began scheming Wang Mi's end.

sentences.zh: 會彌將徐邈輒引部兵去彌，彌漸削弱。

translations.literal: It happened that Mi's general Xu Miao abruptly led his troops away from Mi; Mi gradually weakened.
translations.idiomatic: Then Xu Miao peeled his division away from Wang Mi, leaving the warlord visibly weaker.

sentences.zh: 及勒之獲苟晞也，彌惡之，偽卑辭使謂勒曰：「公獲苟晞而赦之，何其神也！

translations.literal: When Le had captured Gou Xi, Mi resented it; with false humility he sent word to Le, saying, "You captured Gou Xi yet spared him—how divine!"
translations.idiomatic: When Gou Xi fell into Shi Le's hands, Wang Mi bristled yet sent oily praise: "To capture Gou Xi and spare him—only a sage could manage that!"

sentences.zh: 使晞為公左，彌為公右，天下不足定。

translations.literal: "Make Xi your left hand and Mi your right, and the realm is easily settled."
translations.idiomatic: "Put Gou Xi on your left and me on your right, and the empire folds in a month."

sentences.zh: 」勒謂張賓曰：「王彌位重言卑，恐其遂成前狗意也。

translations.literal: Le said to Zhang Bin, "Wang Mi's rank is weighty but his words are humble; I fear he harbours the intent of the dog of old."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le murmured to Zhang Bin, "Wang Mi outranks most lords yet flatters like a petitioner—he reminds me of the cur in the old tale."

sentences.zh: 」賓曰：「觀王公有青州之心，桑梓本邦，固人情之所樂，明公獨無幷州之思乎？

translations.literal: Bin said, "Observing the duke's mind toward Qingzhou—his native soil—surely it is what men love; does the enlightened lord alone have no thought of Bingzhou?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin answered, "He aches for Qingzhou—his home country—who would not? But does Your Grace feel nothing for Bingzhou?

sentences.zh: 王公遲迴未發者，懼明公踵其後，已有規明公之志，但未獲便爾。

translations.literal: The duke tarries and does not set out because he fears the enlightened lord will follow on his heels; he already has intent to measure the enlightened lord, but has not yet found the occasion.
translations.idiomatic: He lingers because he dreads you at his back; he is already sizing you up, only waiting for the moment.

sentences.zh: 今不圖之，恐曹嶷復至，共為羽翼，後雖欲悔，何所及邪！

translations.literal: If we do not plot against him now, I fear Cao Yi will come again, together forming wings; afterward even if we regret it, how can we catch up!
translations.idiomatic: Strike now or Cao Yi will join him and you will face two wings—too late for regrets!

sentences.zh: 徐邈旣去，軍勢稍弱，觀其控御之懷猶盛，可誘而滅之。

translations.literal: Xu Miao has already departed; though his army is slightly weaker, his controlling intent remains strong—he can be lured and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Miao has peeled away part of his strength, yet his arrogance still burns—entice him and you can erase him.

sentences.zh: 」勒以為然。

translations.literal: Le thought it so.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le agreed.

sentences.zh: 勒時與陳午相攻-{于}-蓬關，王彌亦與劉瑞相持甚急。

translations.literal: At the time Le was attacking Chen Wu at Pengguan, and Wang Mi also was locked in stalemate with Liu Rui -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: At the same moment Shi Le besieged Chen Wu at Pengguan while Wang Mi wrestled Liu Rui to a standstill -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 彌請救-{于}-勒，勒未之許。

translations.literal: Mi begged rescue from Le; Le did not grant it -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mi begged for reinforcements; Shi Le stalled -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 張賓進曰：「明公常恐不得王公之便，今天以其便授我矣。

translations.literal: Zhang Bin advanced and said, "The enlightened lord always worried he would not catch the duke's convenience; now Heaven hands us the convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin pressed him, "You have always feared missing your opening against Wang Mi—Heaven has just handed it to you now.

sentences.zh: 陳午小豎，何能為寇？

translations.literal: Chen Wu is a petty boy—what banditry can he work?
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wu is a nobody—what damage could he do?

sentences.zh: 王彌人傑，將為我害。

translations.literal: Wang Mi is a hero among men and will become our harm."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mi is a true champion who will one day be your ruin."

sentences.zh: 」勒因回軍擊瑞，斬之。

translations.literal: Le therefore turned the army, struck Rui, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le spun his host about, fell on Liu Rui, and struck off his head.

sentences.zh: 彌大悅，謂勒深心推奉，無復疑也。

translations.literal: Mi greatly rejoiced, thinking Le deeply supported him, and had no further suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mi rejoiced, convinced that Shi Le honored him, and dropped every guard.

sentences.zh: 勒引師攻陳午-{于}-肥澤，午司馬上黨李頭說勒曰：「公天生神武，當平定四海，四海士庶皆仰屬明公，望濟-{于}-塗炭。

translations.literal: Le led troops to attack Chen Wu -{yu}- at Feize; Wu's marshal Li Tou of Shangdang said to Le, "You were born with divine martialness; you ought to pacify the four seas; scholars and commoners of the four seas all look up to the enlightened lord, hoping to be delivered -{yu}- from mud and charcoal.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le drove on Chen Wu -{yu}- at Feize, where Wu's marshal Li Tou of Shangdang said, "Heaven made you a conqueror; you are meant to pacify the realm, and every scholar and commoner looks to you, begging to be lifted -{yu}- out of the fire and mud.

sentences.zh: 有與公爭天下者，公不早圖之，而返攻我曹流人。

translations.literal: There is one who contends the realm with the enlightened lord; if the enlightened lord does not plot against him early, why instead attack us wandering folk.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you dawdle while another would seize the empire, and instead you grind down homeless exiles like us.

sentences.zh: 我曹鄉黨，終當奉戴，何遽見逼乎！

translations.literal: We, village fellows, will in the end support and obey—why press us so urgently!"
translations.idiomatic: We exiles will one day raise you as our lord—why turn your blades on us now!

sentences.zh: 」勒心然之，詰朝引退。

translations.literal: Le's heart approved; at dawn he led the withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le took the point; at first light he broke camp and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 詭請王彌讌-{于}-已吾，彌長史張嵩諫彌勿就，恐有專諸、孫峻之禍，彌不從。

translations.literal: He falsely invited Wang Mi to a banquet at Yiwu; Mi's chief clerk Zhang Song remonstrated with Mi not to go, fearing the disasters of Zhuan Zhu and Sun Jun; Mi did not follow -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: He invited Wang Mi to a victory feast at Yiwu; Zhang Song warned of assassins like Zhuan Zhu or Sun Jun, but Wang Mi swaggered in anyway -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 旣入，酒酣，勒手斬彌而幷其衆，啟聰稱彌叛逆之狀。

translations.literal: After entering, when wine was heated, Le personally beheaded Mi and annexed his masses, reporting to Cong that Mi had rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-banquet Shi Le drew steel, took Wang Mi's head, swallowed his army, and wrote Liu Cong that Wang Mi had risen in revolt.

sentences.zh: 聰署勒鎮東大將軍、督幷幽二州軍事、領幷州刺史，持節、征討都督、校尉、開府、幽州牧、公如故。

translations.literal: Cong appointed Le grand general who guards the east, supervisor of military affairs for Bing and You two provinces, concurrent inspector of Bingzhou, with staff, campaign commander-in-chief, colonel-in-chief, opened office, shepherd of Youzhou, and duke as before.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong answered with grand general of the east, joint overseer of Bing and You, Bingzhou inspector, full insignia, campaign command, colonel, opened office, Youzhou shepherd, and his ducal patent unchanged.

sentences.zh: 苟晞、王讚謀叛勒，勒害之。

translations.literal: Gou Xi and Wang Zan plotted rebellion against Le; Le killed them.
translations.idiomatic: When Gou Xi and Wang Zan plotted his overthrow, Shi Le killed them both.

sentences.zh: 以將軍左伏肅為前鋒都尉，攻掠豫州諸郡，臨江而還，屯-{于}-葛陂，降諸夷楚，署將軍二千石以下，稅其義穀，以供軍士。

translations.literal: He made the general Zuo Fusu vanguard commandant, raided the commanderies of Yuzhou, reached the river and returned, encamped at Gebei, submitted the various Yi and Chu, appointed generals and two-thousand-bushel officials, levied their surplus grain to supply the soldiers -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: He named Zuo Fusu vanguard commandant to scour Yuzhou, raid to the Great River, and swing back to Gebei, where he enrolled Yi and Chu tribesmen, handed out ranks down to two-thousand-bushel posts, and taxed their grain to feed the army -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 初，勒被鬻平原，與母王相失。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Le had been sold to Pingyuan, he had lost track of his mother Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago, sold into Pingyuan, he had lost his mother Lady Wang.

sentences.zh: 至是，劉琨遣張儒送王-{于}-勒，遺勒書曰：「將軍發迹河朔，席捲兗豫，飲馬江淮，折沖漢沔，雖自古名將，未足為諭。

translations.literal: At this time Liu Kun sent Zhang Ru to deliver Wang to Le, sending a letter to Le saying, "The general rose in Hebei, rolled up Yan and Yu, watered horses on the Yangzi and Huai, and shattered hosts on the Han and Mian—though famed generals of antiquity, none suffice for comparison -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Now Liu Kun sent Zhang Ru escorting Lady Wang back with a letter praising how Shi Le had sprung from the Hebei marshes, scoured Yan and Yu, watered horses on the Yangzi and Huai, and broken hosts on the Han and Mian—surpassing every classic captain -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 所以攻城而不有其人，略地而不有其土，翕爾雲合，忽復星散，將軍豈知其然哉？

translations.literal: Therefore you attack cities yet do not keep their people, seize land yet do not keep the soil; you gather like clouds and suddenly scatter like stars—does the general himself know why?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet you take cities without holding their folk, win ground without holding the soil, swell like a cloud then melt away—do you understand why?"

sentences.zh: 存亡決在得主，成敗要在所附；

translations.literal: Survival and destruction hinge on whom one serves; victory and defeat lie in whom one attaches to.
translations.idiomatic: Survival rides on whom you serve; victory rides on whom you follow."

sentences.zh: 得主則為義兵，附逆則為賊衆。

translations.literal: He who serves the right becomes a righteous host; he who attaches to rebellion becomes a rebel mass.
translations.idiomatic: Serve the right and you lead a righteous army; cling to rebels and you are only bandits."

sentences.zh: 義兵雖敗，而功業必成；

translations.literal: Though a righteous army be defeated, merit and enterprise are sure to be completed;
translations.idiomatic: Even when a loyal army loses a field, its cause can still be brought to completion;

sentences.zh: 賊衆雖克，而終歸殄滅。

translations.literal: though a rebel mass be victorious, in the end it is extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: even a winning rebel ends in ashes."

sentences.zh: 昔赤眉、黃巾橫逆宇宙，所以一旦敗亡者，正以兵出無名，聚而為亂。

translations.literal: In old times the Red Eyebrows and Yellow Turbans ran riot across the universe; the reason they in one morning were defeated and destroyed was precisely that troops went out without a true name and gathered to make chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Remember the Red Eyebrows and Yellow Turbans: they fell because they fought without a just banner and looted like wolves."

sentences.zh: 將軍以天挺之質，威振宇內，擇有德而推崇，隨時望而歸之，勳義堂堂，長享遐貴。

translations.literal: The general, with a quality spanned by Heaven, awe-inspiring within the universe, chooses the virtuous to exalt, follows the timely hope and returns to it—merit and righteousness are radiant, and you long enjoy distant honour.
translations.idiomatic: You were born for command; pick a worthy sovereign, ride the tide, and your righteousness will shine for ages."

sentences.zh: 背聰則禍除，向主則福至。

translations.literal: Turn your back on Cong and disaster is removed; turn toward the sovereign and fortune arrives.
translations.idiomatic: Renounce Liu Cong and danger ends; embrace the Jin throne and fortune returns."

sentences.zh: 採納往誨，翻然改圖，天下不足定，蟻寇不足掃。

translations.literal: Accept the admonitions of the past, turn your plans about with a flip—then the realm is not hard to settle, and ant-like bandits are not hard to sweep.
translations.idiomatic: Heed old counsel, change course, and the realm is yours while gnats like Wang Mi scatter."

sentences.zh: 今相授侍中、持節、車騎大將軍、領護匈奴中郎將、襄城郡公，總內外之任，兼華戎之號，顯封大郡，以表殊能，將軍其受之，副遠近之望也。

translations.literal: Now I invest you as palace attendant, staff-bearing, chariot-and-horse grand general, concurrent colonel of the Xiongnu within the borders, duke of Xiangcheng commandery, overall charge of inner and outer affairs, bearing both Hu and Han titles, with a great commandery enfeoffed to display extraordinary ability—let the general receive it, answering the hopes of near and far."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I offer palace attendant, staff, chariot-and-horse grand general, colonel of the Xiongnu within the borders, duke of Xiangcheng, authority over court and camp, titles for Hu and Han alike, and a fat fief—accept and satisfy every expectation."

sentences.zh: 自古以來誠無戎人而為帝王者，至於名臣建功業者，則有之矣。

translations.literal: From antiquity there has truly been no barbarian man who became Son of Heaven; as for famous ministers who established merit and enterprise, there have been such.
translations.idiomatic: No barbarian has ever truly founded a dynasty, yet many foreign-born ministers have built lasting fame."

sentences.zh: 今之遲想，蓋以天下大亂，當須雄才。

translations.literal: What I ponder at a distance is that because the realm is in great chaos, there must be heroic talent.
translations.idiomatic: I speak plainly because the age demands heroes."

sentences.zh: 遙聞將軍攻城野戰，合於機神，雖不視兵書，闇與孫吳同契，所謂生而知之者上，學而知之者次。

translations.literal: From afar I hear the general in storming cities and field battles matches the spirit of opportunity; though you have not seen the military treatises, tacitly you accord with Sun and Wu—what is called those who know by birth are highest, those who know by study are next.
translations.idiomatic: They say you fight by instinct though you never opened Sunzi—born strategists outrank book-taught men.

sentences.zh: 但得精騎五千，以將軍之才，何向不摧！

translations.literal: But obtain five thousand picked horse—with the general's talent, what direction would not be shattered!
translations.idiomatic: Give me five thousand veterans under your command and every front will break!

sentences.zh: 至心實事，皆張儒所具。

translations.literal: The utmost sincerity and solid facts are all set forth by Zhang Ru."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ru carries every earnest word."

sentences.zh: 」勒報琨曰：「事功殊途，非腐儒所聞。

translations.literal: "Le replied to Kun, saying, "Affairs and merit follow different paths—not what pedantic scholars hear."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le answered Liu Kun, "Worth and policy do not travel the same road—this is beyond a bookworm's hearing."

sentences.zh: 君當逞節本朝，吾自夷，難為效。

translations.literal: You ought to display your integrity toward your court; I am a barbarian and hard put to imitate."
translations.idiomatic: You keep faith with Luoyang; I am a barbarian and a poor copy."

sentences.zh: 」遺琨名馬珍寶，厚賓其使，謝歸以絕之。

translations.literal: "He sent Kun famous horses and treasures, richly rewarded his envoy, declined and sent him back to break relations.
translations.idiomatic: He sent back Liu Kun's gifts of famous steeds and gems, tipped the messenger generously, and closed the correspondence.

sentences.zh: 勒於葛陂繕室宇，課農造舟，將寇建鄴。

translations.literal: At Gebei Le repaired chambers and halls, supervised farming and built boats, intending to raid Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: At Gebei he built halls, drilled farmers, and launched boats aimed at Jianye.

sentences.zh: 會霖雨歷三月不止，元帝使諸將率江南之衆大集壽春，勒軍中-{飢}-疫死者太半。

translations.literal: It happened that unceasing rains lasted more than three months; Emperor Yuan sent generals to mass the hosts of Jiangnan at Shouchun; in Le's army hunger and plague killed more than half -{ji}-.
translations.idiomatic: Then rains fell three months without pause while Emperor Yuan stacked Jiangnan armies at Shouchun; famine and pestilence halved Shi Le's camps -{ji}-.

sentences.zh: 檄書朝夕繼至，勒會諸將計之。

translations.literal: Dispatch letters arrived morning and evening; Le convened generals to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Challenge scrolls arrived hourly until Shi Le called a council of his generals.

sentences.zh: 右長史刁膺諫勒先送款於帝，求掃平河朔，待軍退之後徐更計之。

translations.literal: The right senior clerk Diao Ying remonstrated with Le first to send good faith to the emperor, beg to sweep the Hebei plain, and after the armies withdraw slowly plan again.
translations.idiomatic: Right clerk Diao Ying urged him to sue for peace with Jiankang, offer to pacify Hebei, then replot once the southern armies withdrew.

sentences.zh: 勒愀然長嘯。

translations.literal: Le gave a long whistle, grimacing.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le only scowled and let out a long whistle.

sentences.zh: 中堅夔安勸勒就高避水，勒曰：「將軍何其怯乎！

translations.literal: The central stalwart Kui An urged Le to move to higher ground and avoid the flood; Le said, "General—how fearful you are!"
translations.idiomatic: Kui An, his stalwart champion, begged him to strike for high ground before the floods; Shi Le sneered, "Since when am I a general who flinches?"

sentences.zh: 」孔萇、支雄等三十餘將進曰：「及吳軍未集，萇等請各將三百步卒，乘船三十餘道，夜登其城，斬吳將頭，得其城，食其倉米。

translations.literal: Kong Chang, Zhi Xiong and more than thirty generals advanced and said, "While Wu troops are still gathering, we ask each to take three hundred foot soldiers aboard thirty-odd boats, scale their walls by night, take Wu generals' heads, seize the city, and eat their granary rice."
translations.idiomatic: Kong Chang, Zhi Xiong, and thirty other generals pressed forward: "Before the Eastern Jin armies mass, give each of us three hundred foot and a separate channel of boats—we will scale Jiankang in the dark, behead their commanders, hold the city, and feed the army from their granaries."

sentences.zh: 今年要當破丹陽，定江南，盡生縛取司馬家兒輩。

translations.literal: "This year we mean to break Danyang, secure the south of the Yangzi, and bind every Sima princeling alive."
translations.idiomatic: "This is the year we take Danyang, lock down the southland, and drag every Sima heirling away in ropes."

sentences.zh: 」勒笑曰：「是勇將之計也。

translations.literal: Le laughed and said, "That is a brave general's stratagem."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le laughed. "Brave talk for field captains."

sentences.zh: 」各賜鎧馬一匹。

translations.literal: To each he granted one suit of armour and a horse.
translations.idiomatic: He handed each spokesman a horse and a suit of mail anyway.

sentences.zh: 顧問張賓曰：「於君計何如？

translations.literal: He turned and asked Zhang Bin, "What is your reckoning?"
translations.idiomatic: He wheeled on Zhang Bin. "What do you say?"

sentences.zh: 」賓曰：「將軍攻陷帝都，囚執天子，殺害王侯，妻略妃主，擢將軍之發不足以數將軍之罪，奈何復還相臣奉乎！

translations.literal: Bin said, "The general has stormed the imperial capital, imprisoned the Son of Heaven, butchered kings and nobles, ravaged consorts and princesses—even if we plucked every hair on your head it would not count your crimes—how can you again face about and wish to serve him as minister!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin said coldly, "You have sacked Luoyang, caged the emperor, slaughtered the royal kin, and defiled the harem—pluck every hair from your head and you still could not tally the crimes. And now you dream of bowing again as a Jin minister?"

sentences.zh: 去年誅王彌之後，不宜於此營建。

translations.literal: "After killing Wang Mi last year you ought not to have camped and built here."
translations.idiomatic: "Last year you cut down Wang Mi; you should never have lingered to build here."

sentences.zh: 天降霖雨方數百里中，示將軍不應留也。

translations.literal: "Heaven sends months of rain across hundreds of li—it signals that the general ought not to stay."
translations.idiomatic: "Heaven has washed three hundred li in rain to tell you this is no place to stay."

sentences.zh: 鄴有三臺之固，西接平陽，四塞山河，有喉衿之勢，宜北徙據之。

translations.literal: "Ye has the strength of the Three Terraces, links to Pingyang on the west, is locked by four passes with mountains and rivers—a throat-guard; you ought to shift north and hold it."
translations.idiomatic: "Ye still boasts the Three Terraces, ties to Pingyang, and mountain barriers on every side—the true choke point of the plain. March north and seize it."

sentences.zh: 伐叛懷服，河朔旣定，莫有處將軍之右者。

translations.literal: "Strike rebels and cherish those who submit; once Hebei is settled no one will stand to the general's right."
translations.idiomatic: "Crush every rebel who resists, fold in every band that yields, and once the north is quiet no warlord will dare stand at your shoulder."

sentences.zh: 晉之保壽春，懼將軍之往擊爾，今卒聞迴軍，必欣於敵去，未遑奇兵掎擊也。

translations.literal: "Jin holds Shouchun only because they dread your marching to strike; if they suddenly hear you wheel about they will rejoice the foe is gone and will not trouble to send raiders against your flank."
translations.idiomatic: "The southerners cling to Shouchun because they fear your next blow; hear that you are leaving and they will dance, never dreaming you might snap at their heels."

sentences.zh: 輜重逕從北道，大軍向壽春，輜重旣過，大軍徐迴，何懼進退無地乎！

translations.literal: "Send baggage straight along the northern road while the main host feints toward Shouchun; once the trains are clear, let the army drift back at leisure—why fear having nowhere to advance or withdraw!"
translations.idiomatic: "Run the wagons up the northern track, parade the banners toward Shouchun, then once the supplies are safe, peel away at leisure—no trap can close on you."

sentences.zh: 」勒攘袂鼓髯曰：「賓之計是也。

translations.literal: Le rolled up his sleeves, stroked his beard, and said, "Bin's plan is correct."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le flung back his sleeves, combed his beard, and cried, "Zhang Bin has it!"

sentences.zh: 」責刁膺曰：「君共相輔佐，當規成功業，如何便相勸降！

translations.literal: He rebuked Diao Ying, saying, "You are meant to help me win an empire—how dare you counsel surrender!"
translations.idiomatic: He rounded on Diao Ying. "We are building a realm together—who invited talk of capitulation?"

sentences.zh: 此計應斬。

translations.literal: "This counsel deserves the headsman's axe."
translations.idiomatic: "That advice would cost a man his head."

sentences.zh: 然相明性怯，所以宥君。

translations.literal: "Yet I pardon you, knowing you are timid by nature."
translations.idiomatic: "Still, I spare you—I know fear is your nature."

sentences.zh: 」於是退膺為將軍，擢賓為右長史，加中壘將軍，號曰「右侯」。

translations.literal: Thereupon he demoted Ying to general, raised Bin to right senior clerk, added general of the central bastion, and styled him "Marquis of the Right."
translations.idiomatic: He busted Diao Ying to a line general, raised Zhang Bin to chief clerk on the right, added the central bastion title, and dubbed him the "Marquis of the Right."

sentences.zh: 發自葛陂，遣石季龍率騎二千距壽春。

translations.literal: Setting out from Gebei he sent Shi Jilong with two thousand horse to screen Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: They broke camp at Gebei and Shi Jilong rode ahead with two thousand horsemen to shadow Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 會江南運船至，獲米布數十艘，將士爭之，不設備。

translations.literal: It happened that Jiangnan grain boats arrived; they seized dozens of hulls of rice and cloth; officers and men scrambled for the plunder and posted no pickets.
translations.idiomatic: River barges from the south sailed into their hands—dozens of holds of rice and cloth—and the troops mobbed the cargo like market thieves, never minding sentries.

sentences.zh: 晉伏兵大發，敗季龍-{于}-巨靈口，赴水死者五百餘人，奔退百里，及-{于}-勒軍。

translations.literal: Jin ambush troops sprang forth in force, defeated Jilong at Julingkou, drowned more than five hundred, and routed them a hundred li until they crashed into Le's main host -{yu}- -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Jin ambushers sprang the trap at Julingkou, sank five hundred of Jilong's men in the ford, and chased the survivors a hundred li into Shi Le's main camp -{yu}- -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 軍中震擾，謂王師大至，勒陣以待之。

translations.literal: The army was shaken, thinking the imperial host had come in strength; Le drew up battle lines and waited.
translations.idiomatic: Panic rippled through the ranks until Shi Le steadied them and drew up for a showdown that never came.

sentences.zh: 晉懼有伏兵，退還壽春。

translations.literal: Jin feared further ambushes and withdrew into Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: The southerners, fearing another snare, scuttled back inside Shouchun's walls.

sentences.zh: 勒所過路次，皆堅壁清野，采掠無所獲，軍中大饑，士衆相食。

translations.literal: Everywhere along the line of march walls were strengthened and fields cleared; raiding seized nothing; the army starved terribly; soldiers devoured one another.
translations.idiomatic: Every village had scorched the earth ahead of him; foraging yielded nothing; famine gnawed the column until men fed on men.

sentences.zh: 行達東燕，聞汲郡向冰有衆數千，壁-{于}-枋頭，勒將於棘津北渡，懼冰邀之，會諸將問計。

translations.literal: Marching he reached Eastern Yan; hearing that Xiang Bing of Ji commandery had several thousand men fortifying at Fangtou, Le planned to ford north of Jiji Ford, feared Bing would intercept him, and called generals to ask plans -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Near Dongyan he learned that Xiang Bing of Ji commandery had walled up thousands at Fangtou; Shi Le meant to cross above Jiji Ford but dreaded an ambush, so he called a council of war -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 張賓進曰：「如聞冰船盡在瀆中，未上枋內，可簡壯勇者千人，詭道潛渡，襲取其船，以濟大軍。

translations.literal: Zhang Bin advanced and said, "I hear Bing's boats are still in the sluices and have not been hauled inside Fang—pick a thousand brave men, cross by a hidden track, seize their boats, and ferry the great army."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin said, "Xiang Bing's hulls still sit in the canal, not yet winched behind the wall—slip a thousand raiders across, steal the fleet, and the river is yours."

sentences.zh: 大軍旣濟，冰必可擒也。

translations.literal: "Once the great army is across, Bing can surely be taken."
translations.idiomatic: "Once your main body is over, Xiang Bing is finished."

sentences.zh: 」勒從之，使支雄、孔萇等從文石津縛筏潛渡，勒引其衆自酸棗向棘津。

translations.literal: Le followed it; he had Zhi Xiong and Kong Chang bind rafts at Wenshi Ford and cross secretly; Le led the host from Suanzao toward Jiji Ford.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le agreed: Zhi Xiong and Kong Chang lashed rafts at Wenshi Ford while he drove the army from Suanzao toward Jiji.

sentences.zh: 冰聞勒軍至，始欲內其船。

translations.literal: When Bing heard Le's army had come, he first tried to haul in his boats.
