translations.idiomatic: When Xiang Bing heard Shi Le was closing, he scrambled to pull his boats behind the wall.

sentences.zh: 會雄等已渡，屯其壘門，下船三十餘艘以濟其軍，令主簿鮮-{于}-豐挑戰，設三伏以待之。

translations.literal: It happened that Xiong's men had already crossed, camped at his gate, floated thirty-odd boats to ferry the army, ordered registrar Xianyu Feng to challenge, and laid three ambushes -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Xiong was already ashore, camped at the gate, floated thirty boats to ferry the host, sent registrar Xianyu Feng to shout a challenge, and hid three strikes along the road -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 冰怒，乃出軍，將戰，而三伏齊發，夾擊攻之，又因其資，軍遂豐振。

translations.literal: Bing angrily marched out; as battle was joined the three ambushes rose together, struck from both flanks, and seized his stores; the army's morale surged.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Bing stormed out in fury; the three ambushes hammered him from both flanks, captured his supplies, and the army's spirits soared.

sentences.zh: 長驅寇鄴，攻北中郎將劉演-{于}-三臺。

translations.literal: He drove straight to raid Ye and attacked North Centre Commandant Liu Yan at Santai -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: He raced on Ye and pinned Liu Yan, the North Centre commandant, on Santai terrace -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 演部將臨深、牟穆等率衆數萬降-{于}-勒。

translations.literal: Yan's officers Lin Shen, Mou Mu and others led tens of thousands to submit to Le -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan's lieutenants Lin Shen and Mou Mu brought tens of thousands over to Shi Le -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 時諸將佐議欲攻取三臺以據之，張賓進曰：「劉演衆猶數千，三臺險固，攻守未可卒下，舍之則能自潰。

translations.literal: Counsellor-generals debated storming Santai; Zhang Bin said, "Liu Yan still has several thousand men; the three terraces are steep—storming will not finish quickly; leave him and he will rot on his own."
translations.idiomatic: Staff urged a direct assault on Santai, but Zhang Bin warned, "Liu Yan still holds thousands on those cliffs; a siege will drag; starve him out and he collapses alone."

sentences.zh: 王彭祖、劉越石大敵也，宜及其未有備，密規進據罕城，廣運糧儲，西稟平陽，掃定幷薊，桓文之業可以濟也。

translations.literal: "Wang Pengzu and Liu Yueshi are great foes; strike while they are unprepared, secretly seize Handan city, ship grain widely, submit word west to Pingyang, sweep Bing and Ji—then a Huan-Wen style enterprise can succeed."
translations.idiomatic: "Wang Jun and Liu Kun are the real enemies—move before they expect you, seize Handan, stack grain, report west to Liu Cong, clear Bing and Ji, and you can build a true hegemon's foundation."

sentences.zh: 且今天下鼎沸，戰爭方始，遊行羇旅，人無定志，難以保萬全、制天下也。

translations.literal: "Moreover the realm boils; war has only begun; roaming hosts have no fixed will—hard to guarantee total safety or rule the realm."
translations.idiomatic: "The world is still a cauldron; armies wander without loyalty—you cannot hedge every risk from a camp stool."

sentences.zh: 夫得地者昌，失地者亡。

translations.literal: "He who gains land thrives; he who loses land perishes."
translations.idiomatic: "Land won means strength; land lost means extinction."

sentences.zh: 邯鄲、襄國，趙之舊都，依山憑險，形勝之國，可擇此二邑而都之，然後命將四出，授以奇略，推亡固存，兼弱攻昧，則羣凶可除，王業可圖矣。

translations.literal: "Handan and Xiangguo are Zhao's old capitals, leaning on mountains and defiles—choose one as capital, then send generals on four roads with clever plans, destroy the dying and strengthen the living, swallow the weak and strike the blind—then every villain falls and kingship is within reach."
translations.idiomatic: "Handan and Xiangguo were Zhao's twin seats, ringed by hills—pick one for your capital, fan generals in every direction with ruthless tactics, and you can extirpate rivals and aim at the throne."

sentences.zh: 」勒曰：「右侯之計是也。

translations.literal: Le said, "The right marquis's plan is right."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le said, "Zhang Bin is right again."

sentences.zh: 」於是進據襄國。

translations.literal: Thereupon he advanced and occupied Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: He marched into Xiangguo and made it his seat.

sentences.zh: 賓又言於勒曰：「今我都此，越石、彭祖深所忌也，恐及吾城池未固，資儲未廣，送死於我。

translations.literal: Bin again said to Le, "Now that we hold this place, Yueshi and Pengzu deeply fear us; they may strike before our walls are firm and stores ample."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin added, "Liu Kun and Wang Jun dread this foothold—they may hit you before the ramparts rise and the granaries fill."

sentences.zh: 聞廣平諸縣秋稼大成，可分遣諸將收掠野穀。

translations.literal: "I hear the autumn harvest in Guangping commandery has been abundant; dispatch generals to gather grain from the fields."
translations.idiomatic: "I hear Guangping's autumn crop is heavy—send columns to sweep the countryside for grain."

sentences.zh: 遣使平陽，陳宜鎮此之意。

translations.literal: "Send envoys to Pingyang stating it is fitting to hold this place."
translations.idiomatic: "Write Liu Cong that you mean to hold the north for him."

sentences.zh: 」勒又然之。

translations.literal: Le again approved.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le agreed once more.

sentences.zh: 於是上表于劉聰，分命諸將攻冀州郡縣壘壁，率多降附，運糧以輸勒。

translations.literal: Thereupon he memorialized Liu Cong, ordered generals against stockades in Jizhou—most submitted—and convoys shipped grain to Le.
translations.idiomatic: He tabled Liu Cong, sent raiders through Jizhou's forts—most yielded—and wagon trains began feeding his camps.

sentences.zh: 劉聰署勒使持節、散騎常侍、都督冀幽幷營四州雜夷、征討諸軍事、冀州牧，進封本國上黨郡公，邑五萬戶，開府、幽州牧、東夷校尉如故。

translations.literal: Liu Cong appointed Le bearer of credentials, supernumerary palace attendant, commander of military affairs for Ji, You, Bing, and Ying four regions and miscellaneous Yi, generalissimo of campaigns, shepherd of Jizhou, advanced his ducal fief to Shangdang with fifty thousand households, opened office, kept shepherd of You and colonel of the eastern Yi as before.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong answered with jewelled credentials, palace rank, four-region command, Jizhou shepherd, a fat Shangdang dukedom, fifty thousand households, opened office, and renewed his Youzhou titles.

sentences.zh: 廣平游綸、張豺擁衆數萬，受王浚假署，保據苑鄉。

translations.literal: You Lun and Zhang Cai of Guangping led tens of thousands, received Wang Jun's brevet commission, and held Yuanxiang.
translations.idiomatic: You Lun and Zhang Cai of Guangping mustered tens of thousands under Wang Jun's seal and walled up at Yuanxiang.

sentences.zh: 勒使夔安、支雄等七將攻之，破其外壘。

translations.literal: Le sent Kui An, Zhi Xiong and seven other generals; they broke their outer rampart.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le sent Kui An, Zhi Xiong, and five other generals who shredded their outer wall.

sentences.zh: 浚遣督護王昌及鮮卑段就六眷、末柸、匹磾等部衆五萬餘以討勒。

translations.literal: Jun sent supervisor Wang Chang with Duan Jiulujuan, Moben, Pidi and others—more than fifty thousand Xianbei—to campaign against Le.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun answered with Wang Chang, Duan Jiulujuan, Moben, Pidi, and fifty thousand Xianbei horse.

sentences.zh: 時城隍未修，乃于襄國築隔城重柵，設鄣以待之。

translations.literal: Because city moats were not yet repaired, at Xiangguo he built an inner palisade with doubled stockades and screens to await them.
translations.idiomatic: With ditches still half-dug, he threw up an inner ring of palisades and doubled stockades at Xiangguo to receive them.

sentences.zh: 就六眷屯-{于}-渚陽，勒分遣諸將連出挑戰，頻為就六眷所敗，又聞其大造攻具，勒顧謂其將佐曰：「今寇來轉逼，彼衆我寡，恐攻圍不解，外救不至，內糧罄絕，縱孫吳重生，亦不能固也。

translations.literal: Jiulujuan encamped -{yu}- at Zhuyang; Le repeatedly sent generals to skirmish and was often defeated by Jiulujuan; hearing they were building great siege engines, Le turned to his staff and said, "Now the foe presses closer, they are many and we few—I fear we cannot break the siege, outside relief will not come, inside provisions will fail—even if Sun and Wu were reborn they could not hold."
translations.idiomatic: Duan Jiulujuan camped -{yu}- at Zhuyang; Shi Le's probes kept losing, and when spies reported massive siege gear, he told his captains, "They outnumber us, the ring tightens, no relief is coming, and the bins are low—even Sun Wu reborn could not hold this wall."

sentences.zh: 吾將簡練將士，大陣於野以決之，何如？

translations.literal: "I mean to drill commanders and soldiers and offer grand battle in the open to decide it—what say you?"
translations.idiomatic: "I will sort the ranks and meet them in the field—who is with me?"

sentences.zh: 」諸將皆曰：「宜固守以疲寇，彼師老自退，追而擊之，蔑不克矣。

translations.literal: The generals all said, "We ought to hold firm and weary the foe; when their host is exhausted they will retire of themselves—pursue and strike and none will withstand us."
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "Starve them on the walls until they slink away, then ride them down."

sentences.zh: 」勒顧謂張賓、孔萇曰：「君以為何如」賓、萇俱曰：「聞就六眷剋來月上旬送死北城，其大衆遠來，戰守連日，以我軍勢寡弱，謂不敢出戰，意必懈怠。

translations.literal: Le turned to Zhang Bin and Kong Chang and said, "What do you think?" Bin and Chang together said, "We hear Jiulujuan has set early next month to throw lives against the north wall; his great host has come far, fighting and defending day on day; seeing our army few and weak, they will think we dare not give battle—their minds must slacken."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le looked to Zhang Bin and Kong Chang. "Your view?" Both said, "Jiulujuan plans a dawn rush on the north ramp next month; his tribes have marched far, skirmished daily, and thinks us too weak to sally—already they relax."

sentences.zh: 今段氏種衆之悍，末柸尤最，其卒之精勇，悉在末柸所，可勿復出戰，示之以弱。

translations.literal: "Among the Duan clans' fierce hosts Moben is fiercest; their elite courage is all in Moben's camp—do not answer sorties again, feign weakness."
translations.idiomatic: "The Duan warriors are savage, but Moben packs their best—ignore their taunts and play weak."

sentences.zh: 速鑿北壘為突門二十餘道，候賊列守未定，出其不意，直沖末柸帳，敵必震惶，計不及設，所謂迅雷不及掩耳。

translations.literal: "Quickly cut twenty-odd sally ports through the north ramp; when their lines are not yet set, burst out unexpectedly and drive straight at Moben's tent—the foe will panic and have no plan—that is the thunderclap that gives no time to cover ears."
translations.idiomatic: "Cut twenty hidden sally gates in the north wall; before their ranks set, burst out and spear Moben's yurt—panic will break them faster than thunder."

sentences.zh: 末柸之衆旣奔，餘自摧散。

translations.literal: "Once Moben's mass flees, the rest will collapse of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: "When Moben runs, the whole host unravels."

sentences.zh: 擒末柸之後，彭祖可指辰而定。

translations.literal: "After taking Moben, Wang Pengzu can be fixed within a morning."
translations.idiomatic: "With Moben caged, Wang Jun falls before noon."

sentences.zh: 」勒笑而納之，即以萇為攻戰都督，造突門-{于}-北城。

translations.literal: Le laughed and accepted, immediately making Kong Chang campaign commander for assault and cutting sally ports in the north wall -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le grinned, named Kong Chang master of the storming corps, and tore secret doors through the north palisade -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑入屯北壘，勒候其陣未定，躬率將士鼓噪-{于}-城上。

translations.literal: The Xianbei entered and camped on the north ramp; Le watched their formation unsettled, then personally led officers and men shouting on the wall -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei packed the northern camp; Shi Le waited until their lines sagged, then rode the parapet roaring with his men -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 會孔萇督諸突門伏兵俱出擊之，生擒末柸，就六眷等衆遂奔散。

translations.literal: It happened that Kong Chang led all the sally-port ambushers out together, struck them, and captured Moben alive; Jiulujuan's host then fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Chang blew the sally gates; ambushers swarmed, seized Moben alive, and Jiulujuan's line shattered.

sentences.zh: 萇乘勝追擊，枕-{尸}-三十餘里，獲鎧馬五千匹。

translations.literal: Chang pressed the victory, pursued thirty li with corpses pillowing the road, and took five thousand suits of armour and horses -{shi}-.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Chang chased thirty li of corpse-strewn road and picked up five thousand captured mounts and mails -{shi}-.

sentences.zh: 就六眷收其遺衆，屯-{于}-渚陽，遣使求和，送鎧馬金銀，幷以末柸三弟為質而請末柸。

translations.literal: Jiulujuan gathered the survivors and encamped at Zhuyang, sent envoys suing for peace, presented armour, horses, and gold and silver, and offered Moben's three younger brothers as hostages while begging Moben's return -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Jiulujuan scraped up survivors at Zhuyang, sued for peace with gold, silver, mail, and horses, and offered three younger brothers of Moben as hostages for Moben's release -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 諸將幷勸勒殺末柸以挫之，勒曰：「遼西鮮卑，健國也，與我素無怨讐，為王浚所使耳。

translations.literal: The generals together urged Le to kill Moben to break their spirit; Le said, "Liaoxi Xianbei are a stalwart nation; with me they have never borne hatred—they were moved by Wang Jun."
translations.idiomatic: Captains begged Shi Le to behead Moben to cow the Duan; Shi Le said, "Liaoxi Xianbei are proud warriors with no old grudge against me—they marched for Wang Jun."

sentences.zh: 今殺一人，結怨一國，非計也。

translations.literal: "Now killing one man would seal enmity with a whole state—not a sound plan."
translations.idiomatic: "Murdering one captive would bind an entire realm against us."

sentences.zh: 放之必悅，不復為王浚用矣。

translations.literal: "Release him and they will rejoice and no longer serve Wang Jun."
translations.idiomatic: "Let him go and they will thank us and quit doing Wang Jun's errands."

sentences.zh: 」於是納其質，遣石季龍盟就六眷-{于}-渚陽，結為兄弟，就六眷等引還。

translations.literal: Thereupon he accepted the hostages, sent Shi Jilong to swear brotherhood with Jiulujuan at Zhuyang, and Jiulujuan and the others withdrew -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: He took the hostages, sent Shi Jilong to clasp blood brotherhood with Jiulujuan at Zhuyang, and watched the Duan host pull back -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 使參軍閻綜獻捷於劉聰。

translations.literal: He had adjutant Yan Zong report victory to Liu Cong.
translations.idiomatic: Adjutant Yan Zong carried the victory dispatch to Liu Cong.

sentences.zh: 於是游綸、張豺請降稱籓，勒將襲幽州，務養將士，權宜許之，皆就署將軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon You Lun and Zhang Cai begged to submit as vassals; Le intended to raid Youzhou, wished to rest soldiers, and provisionally granted it, appointing them all generals.
translations.idiomatic: You Lun and Zhang Cai offered vassalage; Shi Le, saving strength for a strike on Youzhou, accepted and brevetted them generals.

sentences.zh: 於是遣衆寇信都，害冀州刺史王象。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent forces to raid Xindu and killed Jizhou inspector Wang Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He swung columns into Xindu and killed Jizhou inspector Wang Xiang.

sentences.zh: 王浚復以邵舉行冀州刺史，保-{于}-信都。

translations.literal: Jun again made Shao Ju acting Jizhou inspector and held Xindu -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun named Shao Ju acting Jizhou shepherd to hold Xindu -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: ，石季龍攻鄴三臺，鄴潰，劉演奔-{于}-稟丘，將軍謝胥、田青、郎牧等率三臺流人降-{于}-勒，勒以桃豹為魏郡太守以撫之。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Shi Jilong stormed Ye's three terraces; Ye collapsed; Liu Yan fled to Linqiu; generals Xie Xu, Tian Qing, Lang Mu and others led the displaced people of the three terraces to submit to Le; Le made Tao Bao prefect of Wei commandery to soothe them -{yu}- -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jilong shattered Ye's three terraces; Liu Yan bolted to Linqiu; Xie Xu, Tian Qing, Lang Mu, and the refugee garrison of the terraces capitulated; Shi Le set Tao Bao over Wei commandery to calm them -{yu}- -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 命段末柸為子，署為使持節、安北將軍、北平公，遣還遼西。

translations.literal: He took Duan Moben as a foster son, appointed him bearer of credentials, general who pacifies the north, duke of Beiping, and sent him back to Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: He adopted Moben as a son, titled him general who pacifies the north and duke of Beiping, and sent him home to Liaoxi with credentials.

sentences.zh: 末柸感勒厚恩，在途日南面而拜者三，段氏遂專心歸附，自是王浚威勢漸衰。

translations.literal: Moben was moved by Le's great kindness; on the road he bowed toward the south three times each day; the Duan clan thereafter devotedly attached, and from this Wang Jun's might gradually waned.
translations.idiomatic: Moben kowtowed southward thrice daily out of gratitude; the Duan clan swung hard to Shi Le, and Wang Jun's prestige began to ebb.

sentences.zh: 勒襲苑鄉，執遊綸以為主簿。

translations.literal: He raided Yuanxiang and seized You Lun, appointing him chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He struck Yuanxiang, bagged You Lun, and made him chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 攻乞活李惲-{于}-上白，斬之，將坑其降卒，見郭敬而識之，曰：「汝郭季子乎？

translations.literal: He attacked the Qihuo leader Li Yun -{yu}- at Shangbai, beheaded him, and was about to bury the surrendered soldiers alive when he saw Guo Jing, recognized him, and said, "Are you not Guo Jizi?"
translations.idiomatic: He stormed the Qihuo stronghold -{yu}- at Shangbai, killed Li Yun, and was ready to entomb the captives when he spotted Guo Jing in the crowd and cried, "Is that you, Guo Jizi?"

sentences.zh: 」敬叩頭曰：「是也。

translations.literal: Jing knocked his head and said, "It is I."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jing kowtowed. "It is your old friend."

sentences.zh: 」勒下馬執其手，泣曰：「今日相遇，豈非天邪！

translations.literal: Le dismounted, grasped his hand, wept, and said, "To meet today—is it not Heaven's will!"
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le leapt down, seized his hands, and wept, "If this is not fate, what else could it be!"

sentences.zh: 」賜衣服車馬，署敬上將軍，悉免降者以配之。

translations.literal: He granted clothing, chariot, and horses, appointed Jing supreme general, and spared all the surrendered to attach to him.
translations.idiomatic: He draped him in silks, gave him mounts, named him supreme general, and freed every prisoner to serve under him.

sentences.zh: 其將孔萇寇定陵，害兗州刺史田徵。

translations.literal: His general Kong Chang raided Dingling and killed Yanzhou inspector Tian Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Chang swept Dingling and cut down Yanzhou inspector Tian Zheng.

sentences.zh: 烏丸薄盛執渤海太守劉旣，率戶五千降-{于}-勒。

translations.literal: The Wuhuan Bo Sheng seized Bohai prefect Liu Ji, led five thousand households, and submitted to Le -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuan chief Bo Sheng arrested Bohai prefect Liu Ji and delivered five thousand households to Shi Le -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 劉聰授勒侍中、征東大將軍，餘如故，拜其母王氏為上黨國太夫人，妻劉氏上黨國夫人，章綬首飾一同王妃。

translations.literal: Liu Cong appointed Le palace attendant and grand general who campaigns east, the rest as before, ennobled his mother Lady Wang as grand lady of the Shangdang state, his wife Lady Liu as lady of the Shangduguo state, with seals and regalia matching a royal consort.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong added palace attendant and eastern general to his old titles, raised Lady Wang to grand dame of Shangdang, Lady Liu to dame of Shangdang, with queenly insignia.

sentences.zh: 段末柸任弟亡歸遼西，勒大怒，所經令尉皆殺之。

translations.literal: Moben's pledged younger brother fled back to Liaoxi; Le was furious and put every magistrate and captain along the route to death.
translations.idiomatic: When Moben's hostage brother bolted for Liaoxi, Shi Le flew into a rage and executed every county officer along the road.

sentences.zh: 烏丸審廣、漸裳、郝襲背王浚，密遣使降-{于}-勒，勒厚加撫納。

translations.literal: The Wuhuan Shen Guang, Jian Shang, and Hao Xi turned against Wang Jun and secretly sent envoys to submit to Le, who richly comforted and accepted them -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Guang, Jian Shang, and Hao Xi of the Wuhuan broke with Wang Jun, slipped messengers to Shi Le, and found generous terms -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 司冀漸寧，人始租賦。

translations.literal: Si and Ji gradually grew quiet and people began paying rent and tax.
translations.idiomatic: Si and Ji calmed enough that farmers once more paid grain and cloth.

sentences.zh: 立太學，簡明經善書吏署為文學掾，選將佐子弟三百人教之。

translations.literal: He founded an imperial academy, selected clerks versed in the classics and good calligraphy as literary adjutants, and taught three hundred sons of officers.
translations.idiomatic: He opened a school, picked literate clerks for literary posts, and drilled three hundred sons of his captains in the classics.

sentences.zh: 勒母王氏死，潛窆山谷，莫詳其所。

translations.literal: Le's mother Lady Wang died; he secretly buried her in a mountain valley; none knew the place.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang died; Shi Le hid her coffin in a nameless gorge so no enemy could desecrate it.

sentences.zh: 旣而備九命之禮，虛葬-{于}-襄國城南。

translations.literal: Later he staged the full nine-rank rites and held a hollow burial south of Xiangguo city -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Later he staged the ninefold mourning and stacked an empty tomb south of Xiangguo for show -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 勒謂張賓曰：「鄴，魏之舊都，吾將營建。

translations.literal: Le said to Zhang Bin, "Ye is Wei's old capital; I intend to build there."
translations.idiomatic: He told Zhang Bin, "Ye was Cao Wei's seat—I mean to rebuild it."

sentences.zh: 旣風俗殷雜，須賢望以綏之，誰可任也？

translations.literal: "Now customs are thick and mixed; we need worthy prestige to soothe them—whom can we appoint?"
translations.idiomatic: "The place is a babel of peoples; who has the stature to govern it?"

sentences.zh: 」賓曰：「晉故東萊太守南陽趙彭忠亮篤敏，有佐時良榦，將軍若任之，必能允副神規。

translations.literal: Bin said, "Zhao Peng of Nanyang, former prefect of Donglai under Jin, is loyal, bright, and diligent, with talent to aid the age—if the general employs him he will match your divine design."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin named Zhao Peng of Nanyang, once Jin's Donglai prefect—loyal, shrewd, and seasoned—"Give him Ye and the city will obey."

sentences.zh: 」勒於是徵彭，署為魏郡太守。

translations.literal: Thereupon he summoned Peng and appointed him prefect of Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le summoned Zhao Peng and named him Wei prefect.

sentences.zh: 彭至，入泣而辭曰：「臣往策名晉室，食其祿矣。

translations.literal: When Peng arrived he entered weeping and declined, saying, "Your servant formerly pledged his name to the Jin house and ate its salary."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Peng arrived weeping and said, "I once swore myself to the Jin court and took its pay."

sentences.zh: 犬馬戀主，切不敢忘。

translations.literal: "Hound and horse love their master; I dare not forget in my heart."
translations.idiomatic: "Like the emperor's hounds, I cannot forget my first lord."

sentences.zh: 誠知晉之宗廟鞠為茂草，亦猶洪川東逝，往而不還。

translations.literal: "I know indeed the Jin ancestral shrines have turned to rank grass, yet it is like a great river flowing east—gone and not returning."
translations.idiomatic: "I know Luoyang's temples are weed fields, yet it is like a river eastward—gone forever."

sentences.zh: 明公應符受命，可謂攀龍之會。

translations.literal: "The enlightened lord has answered the tallies and received the mandate—this may be called the meeting to mount the dragon."
translations.idiomatic: "You already hold heaven's warrant—this should be every scholar's moment to rise with the dragon."

sentences.zh: 但受人之榮，復事二姓，臣志所不為，恐亦明公之所不許。

translations.literal: "Yet having eaten Jin's honour, to serve a second surname is what my resolve will not do—I fear it is also what the enlightened lord will not permit."
translations.idiomatic: "But having eaten Jin's salary I will not serve a second dynasty—surely that is barred even for you."

sentences.zh: 若賜臣餘年、全臣一介之願者，明公大造之惠也。

translations.literal: "If you grant your servant remaining years and fulfil this one stubborn wish, it is the enlightened lord's supreme grace."
translations.idiomatic: "Spare my life and honour this one foolish wish—that would be mercy beyond measure."

sentences.zh: 」勒默然。

translations.literal: Le was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le said nothing.

sentences.zh: 張賓進曰：「自將軍神旗所經，衣冠之士靡不變節，未有能以大義進退者。

translations.literal: Zhang Bin advanced and said, "Wherever the general's banner has passed, gentry without exception have changed allegiance—none has yet advanced or withdrawn on great righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin murmured, "Every gentleman you meet has bent the knee; none has yet stood on principle before you."

sentences.zh: 至如此賢，以將軍為高祖，自擬為四公，所謂君臣相知，此亦足成將軍不世之高，何必吏之。

translations.literal: "For such a worthy to take the general as his Gaozu and liken himself to the Four Dukes—what is called ruler and minister knowing each other—this too completes the general's unmatched eminence; why must he merely hold office?"
translations.idiomatic: "A man that fine hails you as his Gaozu and ranks himself with the ancient four ministers—that is the bond of true ruler and vassal, glory enough without a clerk's title."

sentences.zh: 」勒大悅，曰：「右侯之言得孤心矣。

translations.literal: Le greatly rejoiced and said, "The right marquis's words have reached the core of my solitary heart."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le beamed. "Zhang Bin has read my mind."

sentences.zh: 」於是賜安車駟馬，養以卿祿，辟其子明為參軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon he granted a secure carriage and four-horse team, maintained him on ministerial salary, and summoned his son Ming as adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: He gave Zhao Peng a cushioned carriage, minister's stipend, and took his son Zhao Ming onto staff.

sentences.zh: 勒以石季龍為魏郡太守，鎮鄴三臺，季龍篡奪之萌兆-{于}-此矣。

translations.literal: Le made Shi Jilong prefect of Wei commandery to guard Ye's three terraces—the first sprout of Jilong's later usurpation sprouted here. -{yu}-
translations.idiomatic: He posted Shi Jilong at Ye's three terraces as Wei prefect—the first hint of the tiger son's future coup. -{yu}-

sentences.zh: 時王浚署置百官，奢縱淫虐，勒有吞幷之意，欲先遣使以觀察之。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Jun had installed a full bureaucracy, indulged luxury, wantonness, and cruelty; Le harboured intent to swallow him and wished first to send envoys to observe him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun ran a shadow court, wallowed in cruelty, and Shi Le meant to devour him—but wanted envoys to test the waters first.

sentences.zh: 議者僉曰：「宜如羊祜與陸抗書相聞。

translations.literal: Counsellors all said, "It should be like Yang Hu's letters to Lu Kang—exchanging courtesies across the lines."
translations.idiomatic: Advisers urged polite letters in the manner of Yang Hu and Lu Kang.

sentences.zh: 」時張賓有疾，勒就而謀之。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Bin was ill; Le went to his couch to consult him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin lay sick, so Shi Le took counsel at his bedside.

sentences.zh: 賓曰：「王浚假三部之力，稱制南面，雖曰晉籓，實懷僭逆之志，必思協英雄，圖濟事業。

translations.literal: Bin said, "Wang Jun leans on the strength of three divisions, styles himself regent facing south; though he calls himself a Jin vassal, in truth he harbours usurping intent—he is sure to wish to align heroes to accomplish the deed."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin said, "Wang Jun rides three Xianbei hosts and plays regent—nominally a Jin vassal, actually a usurper hunting allies."

sentences.zh: 將軍威聲震-{于}-海內，去就為存亡，所在為輕重，浚之欲將軍，猶楚之招韓信也。

translations.literal: "The general's martial name shakes within the seas; to go or stay means life or death for others, wherever you stand tips the scales—Jun's desire to win the general is like Chu summoning Han Xin." -{yu}-
translations.idiomatic: "Your name shakes the realm; every army rises or falls on your nod—Wang courts you the way Chu once courted Han Xin." -{yu}-

sentences.zh: 今權譎遣使，無誠款之形，脫生猜疑，圖之兆露，後雖奇略，無所設也。

translations.literal: "If we now send crafty envoys without showing sincere good faith, suspicion may arise and the omen of our plot be exposed—afterward even clever stratagems have nowhere to apply."
translations.idiomatic: "Trick envoys without real deference and he will smell the plot—then no scheme will save us."

sentences.zh: 夫立大事者必先為之卑，當稱籓推奉，尚恐未信，羊、陸之事，臣未見其可。

translations.literal: "Now he who raises a great matter must first humble himself—he ought to style himself vassal and push devotion; even then trust may fail—I have not seen the Yang Hu–Lu Kang model as workable."
translations.idiomatic: "Great enterprises begin in self-abasement: call yourself his vassal and flatter him, yet even that may not win belief—the Yang Hu and Lu Kang exchange is no sure model."

sentences.zh: 」勒曰：「右侯之計是也。

translations.literal: Le said, "The right marquis's plan is correct."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le said, "Zhang Bin is right."

sentences.zh: 」乃遣其舍人王子春、董肇等多齎珍寶，奉表推崇浚為天子曰：「勒本小胡，出於戎裔，值晉綱弛禦，海內饑亂，流離屯厄，竄命冀州，共相帥合，以救性命。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent his attendants Wang Zichun, Dong Zhao and others bearing many treasures, presenting a memorial that exalted Jun as Son of Heaven, saying, "Le was originally a petty Hu from barbarian stock; encountering the Jin net slackened and the realm famine-stricken, in wandering hardship I fled my life to Jizhou and banded together with others merely to save our lives."
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Wang Zichun and Dong Zhao laden with gems and a memorial that crowned Wang Jun Son of Heaven, claiming Shi Le was a petty barbarian who, when Jin's reins slackened and famine tore the realm, fled to Jizhou and banded with others only to survive.

sentences.zh: 今晉祚淪夷，遠播吳會，中原無主，蒼生無系。

translations.literal: "Now the Jin mandate is cast down and scattered far to Wu and Kuaiji; the Central Plain has no master; the black-haired people have nothing to cling to."
translations.idiomatic: "Jin's mandate is broken, the court chased to the southeast, the heartland lacks a sovereign, and the people have no polestar."

sentences.zh: 伏惟明公殿下，州鄉貴望，四海所宗，為帝王者，非公復誰？

translations.literal: "We humbly consider the enlightened duke, honoured in province and village, the cynosure of the four seas—who else under Heaven could be Son of Heaven if not you?"
translations.idiomatic: "You, Duke, are the north's great name and the world's lodestar—who else could wear the crown?"

sentences.zh: 勒所以捐軀命、興義兵誅暴亂者，正為明公驅除爾。

translations.literal: "The reason Le has given body and life and raised righteous troops to slaughter tyranny is precisely to clear the way for the enlightened duke."
translations.idiomatic: "I have wagered my life on these arms only to sweep the path for you."

sentences.zh: 伏願殿下應天順時，踐登皇阼。

translations.literal: "We humbly hope the duke will answer Heaven and the season, mount the imperial stairs, and ascend."
translations.idiomatic: "Take heaven's hint, seize the moment, and mount the throne."

sentences.zh: 勒奉戴明公，如天地父母，明公當察勒微心，慈眄如子也。

translations.literal: "Le supports the enlightened duke like Heaven and earth and father and mother; the duke ought to discern Le's humble heart and look on me with kindly favour as on a son."
translations.idiomatic: "I will serve you as child serves parents—only look on me with mercy."

sentences.zh: 」亦遺棗嵩書而厚賂之。

translations.literal: He also sent letters to Zao Song and richly bribed him.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Zao Song separately and greased his palm with gold.

sentences.zh: 浚謂子春等曰：「石公一時英武，據趙舊都，成鼎峙之勢，何為稱籓於孤，其可信乎？

translations.literal: Jun said to Zichun and the others, "Shi Le is for the moment a hero and warrior; he holds Zhao's old capital and forms a tripod stance—why should he style himself vassal to me—can it be believed?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun asked his envoys, "Shi Le is a lion who holds old Zhao in a tripod—why would he bow to me? Can this be real?"

sentences.zh: 」子春對曰：「石將軍英才儁拔，士馬雄盛，實如聖旨。

translations.literal: Zichun replied, "General Shi's talent is outstanding, his soldiers and horses mighty—indeed as your sacred words say."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zichun answered, "Shi Le's genius and his hosts are everything you say—mighty as an edict proclaims."

sentences.zh: 仰惟明公州鄉貴望，累葉重光，出鎮籓嶽，威聲播-{于}-八表，固以胡越欽風，戎夷歌德，豈唯區區小府而敢不斂衽神闕者乎！

translations.literal: "We look up to the enlightened duke's honoured name in province and village, glory piled generation on generation, guarding the great fiefs—his martial name spreads within the eight outer zones; naturally Hu and Yue admire his wind, barbarians sing his virtue—how could a mere petty prefecture dare not gather his lapels before the divine palace!" -{yu}-
translations.idiomatic: "Your name towers across generations of border command; your fame shakes the eight directions—barbarians hymn your virtue. No petty officer would dare withhold reverence." -{yu}-

sentences.zh: 昔陳嬰豈其鄙王而不王，韓信薄帝而不帝者哉？

translations.literal: "In old days did Chen Ying despise kingship and therefore not be king, or Han Xin scorn emperorship and therefore not be emperor?"
translations.idiomatic: "Did Chen Ying scorn the crown, or Han Xin refuse the throne?"

sentences.zh: 但以知帝王不可以智力爭故也。

translations.literal: "It is only because they knew emperorship cannot be wrestled by wit and force alone."
translations.idiomatic: "They knew the mandate is not won by clever force alone."

sentences.zh: 石將軍之擬明公，猶陰精之比太陽，江河之比洪海爾。

translations.literal: "General Shi's comparison of the enlightened duke is like the yin essence beside the sun, like rivers beside the great sea."
translations.idiomatic: "Shi Le ranks you beside the sun and the ocean—himself only moonlight and streams."

sentences.zh: 項籍、子陽覆車不遠，是石將軍之明鑒，明公亦何怪乎！

translations.literal: "Xiang Yu and Gongsun Yang overturned their chariots not long ago—this is General Shi's bright mirror—why should the enlightened duke find it strange!"
translations.idiomatic: "Xiang Yu's crash is still fresh—Shi Le takes it as his mirror. Why doubt him?"

sentences.zh: 且自古誠胡人而為名臣者實有之，帝王則未之有也。

translations.literal: "Moreover from antiquity there have truly been barbarian men who became famous ministers; as for emperors, there have not been such."
translations.idiomatic: "Foreigners have risen to be great ministers; none has founded a dynasty."

sentences.zh: 石將軍非所以惡帝王而讓明公也，顧取之不為天人之所許耳。

translations.literal: "General Shi does not therefore despise emperorship and yield to the enlightened duke—only he sees that seizing it would not win the approval of Heaven and men."
translations.idiomatic: "Shi Le yields the throne not from contempt but because Heaven would not bless the seizure."

sentences.zh: 願公勿疑。

translations.literal: "We hope the duke will not doubt."
translations.idiomatic: "Put doubt aside."

sentences.zh: 」浚大悅，封子春等為列侯，遣使報勒，答以方物。

translations.literal: Jun greatly rejoiced, enfeoffed Zichun and others as rank marquises, sent envoys to answer Le, and returned local tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun was delighted, made the envoys full marquises, sent return gifts, and showered Shi Le with curios.

sentences.zh: 浚司馬游統時鎮范陽，陰叛浚，馳使降-{于}-勒。

translations.literal: Jun's marshal You Tong at the time garrisoned Fanyang; he secretly rebelled against Jun, galloped envoys to surrender to Le -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun's marshal You Tong, holding Fanyang, plotted defection and sent riders to Shi Le -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 勒斬其使，送-{于}-浚，以表誠實。

translations.literal: Le beheaded his envoys and sent the heads to Jun to display good faith -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le executed the couriers and shipped their heads to Wang Jun as proof of loyalty -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 浚雖不罪統，彌信勒之忠誠，無復疑矣。

translations.literal: Though Jun did not punish Tong, he trusted Le's sincerity ever more and had no further doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun spared You Tong yet trusted Shi Le utterly.

sentences.zh: 子春等與王浚使至，勒命匿勁卒精甲，虛府羸師以示之，北面拜使而受浚書。

translations.literal: When Zichun and others arrived with Wang Jun's envoys, Le ordered picked troops and fine armour hidden, emptied his headquarters and showed weak troops, bowed north to the envoys and received Jun's letter.
translations.idiomatic: When the embassy arrived, Shi Le hid his veterans, paraded feeble conscripts, kowtowed north, and accepted Wang Jun's rescript with theatrical awe.

sentences.zh: 浚遺勒麈尾，勒偽不敢執，懸之-{于}-壁，朝夕拜之，-{云}-：「我不得見王公，見王公所賜如見公也。

translations.literal: Jun sent Le a fly-whisk; Le feigned not daring to hold it, hung it on the wall, bowed morning and evening, saying, "I cannot see the duke; seeing the duke's gift is like seeing the duke." -{yu}- -{yun}-
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun sent a yak-tail chowry; Shi Le pretended it was too sacred to touch, hung it like an icon, and worshipped it daily, swearing the whisk was Wang Jun himself -{yu}- -{yun}-.

sentences.zh: 」復遣董肇奉表-{于}-浚，期親詣幽州奉上尊號，亦修箋-{于}-棗嵩，乞幷州牧、廣平公，以見必信之誠也。

translations.literal: He again sent Dong Zhao to present a memorial to Jun, setting a date to go in person to Youzhou to offer the exalted title, and also wrote Zao Song begging shepherd of Bingzhou and duke of Guangping to show utter good faith -{yu}- -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: He had Dong Zhao promise to crown Wang Jun in person at Youzhou and bribed Zao Song with a plea for Bingzhou shepherd and duke of Guangping to seal the bluff -{yu}- -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 勒將圖浚，引子春問之。

translations.literal: Le was about to plot against Jun and summoned Zichun to question him.
translations.idiomatic: As he prepared to strike Youzhou, Shi Le called Wang Zichun for intelligence.

sentences.zh: 子春曰：「幽州自去歲大水，人不粒食，浚積粟百萬，不能贍恤，刑政苛酷，賦役殷煩，賊憲賢良，誅斥諫士，下不堪命，流叛略盡。

translations.literal: Zichun said, "Since last year Youzhou has suffered great flood; people have no grain to eat; Jun has stored a million bushels of grain yet cannot relieve them; punishments are harsh and cruel, taxes and corvée oppressive; worthy men are slandered and remonstrators executed; the lower folk cannot endure and have largely fled or rebelled."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zichun reported floods, hoarded grain unused, cruel law, crushing taxes, murdered advisers, and a population in flight.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑、烏丸離貳-{于}-外，棗嵩、田嶠貪暴-{于}-內，人情沮擾，甲士羸弊。

translations.literal: Xianbei and Wuhuan are divided without; Zao Song and Tian Jiao are greedy and violent within; hearts are shaken and mail-clad soldiers wasted -{yu}- -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei and Wuhuan chiefs feud outwardly while Zao Song and Tian Jiao loot within; morale curdles and armour rusts -{yu}- -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 而浚猶置立臺閣，布列百官，自言漢高、魏武不足並也。

translations.literal: Yet Jun still erects terrace offices and arrays the hundred officials, claiming that even Han Gaozu and Wei Wu cannot match him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wang Jun builds phantom ministries and boasts he outshines Gaozu and Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 又幽州謠怪特甚，聞者莫不為之寒心，浚意氣自若，曾無懼容，此亡期之至也。

translations.literal: Moreover Youzhou's omens and prodigies are extreme; hearers none but shudder—yet Jun's spirit and bearing remain as before, utterly without fear—this is the arrival of his term of death.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhou fills with dread portents while Wang Jun struts unafraid—the hour of his fall has struck.

sentences.zh: 」勒撫-{几}-笑曰：「王彭祖真可擒也。

translations.literal: Le stroked the table and laughed, saying, "Wang Pengzu can truly be seized." -{ji}-
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le rapped his desk and laughed. "Wang Pengzu is ours for the taking." -{ji}-

sentences.zh: 」浚使達幽州，具陳勒形勢寡弱，款誠無二。

translations.literal: When Jun's envoys reached Youzhou they exhaustively described Le's forces as few and weak and his good faith as undivided.
translations.idiomatic: His own envoys painted Shi Le as feeble and utterly sincere.

sentences.zh: 浚大悅，以勒為信然。

translations.literal: Jun greatly rejoiced and believed Le trustworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun swallowed every word.

sentences.zh: 勒纂兵戒期，將襲浚，而懼劉琨及鮮卑、烏丸為其後患，沈吟未發。

translations.literal: Le gathered troops and set a date, intending to raid Jun, yet feared Liu Kun together with Xianbei and Wuhuan as troubles behind him, and hesitated without moving.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le massed men for Youzhou yet dreaded Liu Kun and the steppe peoples at his back, and stalled.

sentences.zh: 張賓進曰：「夫襲敵國，當出其不意。

translations.literal: Zhang Bin advanced, saying, "When raiding an enemy state, one must strike beyond expectation."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin said, "Surprise is the soul of a raid."

sentences.zh: 軍嚴經日不行，豈顧有三方之慮乎？

translations.literal: The army has been drawn up for days without marching—could you be worrying about threats on three sides?"
translations.idiomatic: Armies stand ready day after day—are three-front worries freezing you?"

sentences.zh: 」勒曰：「然，為之奈何？

translations.literal: Le said, "It is so—what shall we do about it?"
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le admitted it. "Then what?"

sentences.zh: 」賓曰：「彭祖之據幽州，唯仗三部，今皆離叛，還為寇讐，此則外無聲援以抗我也。

translations.literal: Bin said, "Pengzu's hold on Youzhou relies solely on the three divisions; now all have split and rebelled, turning into foes—thus without he has no allies to resist us."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin answered, "Wang Jun leans on three Xianbei hosts—now each chief turns on him, so he has no allies outside."

sentences.zh: 幽州-{飢}-儉，人皆蔬食，衆叛親離，甲旅寡弱，此則內無強兵以禦我也。

translations.literal: Youzhou is stricken with famine; people all eat greens; masses rebel and kin depart; mail troops are few and weak—thus within he has no strong army to withstand us -{ji}-.
translations.idiomatic: Famine empties Youzhou, mutiny hollows his halls, and his mail is thin—no inner shield either." -{ji}-

sentences.zh: 若大軍在郊，必土崩瓦解。

translations.literal: If the great army reaches the suburbs, they will surely crumble like earth and tile.
translations.idiomatic: Bring the host to his walls and he collapses like mud.

sentences.zh: 今三方未靖，將軍便能懸軍千里以征幽州也。

translations.literal: Now the three fronts are not yet quiet, yet the general can suspend an army a thousand li to campaign against Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Though three sides still simmer, you can still march a thousand li on Youzhou."

sentences.zh: 輕軍往返，不出二旬。

translations.literal: A light army out and back will not exceed twenty days.
translations.idiomatic: A flying column returns inside twenty days."

sentences.zh: 就使三方有動，勢足旋趾。

translations.literal: Even if the three fronts stir, the situation is enough to wheel about.
translations.idiomatic: If other fronts flare, you can still pivot in time."

sentences.zh: 宜應機電發，勿後時也。

translations.literal: You ought to answer the moment like lightning—do not lag behind the hour."
translations.idiomatic: Strike like lightning—do not miss the hour."

sentences.zh: 且劉琨、王浚雖同名晉籓，其實仇敵。

translations.literal: Moreover Liu Kun and Wang Jun, though both are called Jin vassals, in truth are mutual foes.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun and Wang Jun both wear Jin colors yet hate each other."

sentences.zh: 若修牋-{于}-琨，送質請和，琨必欣-{于}-得我，喜-{于}-浚滅，終不救浚而襲我也。

translations.literal: If you send a letter to Kun, deliver hostages and sue for peace, Kun will surely rejoice at winning us and delight in Jun's destruction—he will not rescue Jun in the end but strike at us." -{yu}- -{yu}- -{yu}-
translations.idiomatic: Write Liu Kun, send hostages, sue for peace—he will cheer our friendship and toast Wang Jun's ruin, never riding to his rescue." -{yu}- -{yu}- -{yu}-

sentences.zh: 」勒曰：「吾所不了，右侯已了，復何疑哉！」

translations.literal: Le said, "What I could not settle, the right marquis has settled—what doubt remains!"
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le cried, "Zhang Bin has settled what baffled me—no more doubt!"

sentences.zh: 於是輕騎襲幽州，以火宵行。

translations.literal: Thereupon with light horse he raided Youzhou, marching by night with torches.
translations.idiomatic: He took light cavalry against Youzhou, torches lit through the nights.

sentences.zh: 至柏人，殺主簿遊綸，以其兄統在范陽，懼聲軍計故也。

translations.literal: Reaching Bairen he killed chief clerk You Lun because Lun's elder brother Tong was at Fanyang, fearing he would leak the army's plan.
translations.idiomatic: At Bairen he executed registrar You Lun lest his brother You Tong in Fanyang betray the march.

sentences.zh: 遣張慮奉牋-{于}-劉琨，陳己過沉重，求討浚以自效。

translations.literal: He sent Zhang Lu presenting a letter to Liu Kun, confessing deep faults and begging to campaign against Jun to prove merit -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lu carried a groveling letter to Liu Kun, begging leave to punish Wang Jun -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 琨旣素疾浚，乃檄諸州郡，說勒知命思愆，收累年之咎，求拔幽都，效善將來，今聽所請，受任通和。

translations.literal: Kun had long hated Jun; therefore he ordered commanderies and prefectures with a proclamation saying Le knew fate and repented guilt, gathering years of fault, begged to uproot the You capital and show good conduct hereafter—now he heard the request and granted alliance and passage.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun, who loathed Wang Jun, broadcast orders that Shi Le repented and meant to tear Youzhou down—he blessed the campaign and opened the road.

sentences.zh: 軍達易水，浚督護孫緯馳遣白浚，將引軍距勒，遊統禁之。

translations.literal: When the army reached Yishui, Jun's protector Sun Wei galloped word to Jun and wished to lead troops to block Le; You Tong forbade it.
translations.idiomatic: At Yishui Wang Jun's adjutant Sun Wei raced a warning, but You Tong blocked mobilization.

sentences.zh: 浚將佐咸請出擊勒，浚怒曰：「石公來，正欲奉戴我也，敢言擊者斬！

translations.literal: Jun's generals all begged to go out and strike Le; Jun angrily said, "Lord Shi is coming precisely to support me—whoever speaks of striking shall be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun's captains begged to fight; Wang Jun roared that Shi Le came to honour him and threatened beheading.

sentences.zh: 」乃命設饗以待之。

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered a feast prepared to await him.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered a banquet laid to welcome his "ally."

sentences.zh: 勒晨至薊，叱門者開門。

translations.literal: Le at dawn reached Ji and shouted at the gatekeepers to open the gates.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Shi Le thundered at Ji's gates until they opened.

sentences.zh: 疑有伏兵，先驅牛羊數千頭，聲言上禮，實欲填諸街巷，使兵不得發。

translations.literal: Fearing ambush, he first drove several thousand head of sheep and cattle, claiming they were tribute gifts, but in truth wished to fill the lanes and alleys so troops could not deploy.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing ambush, he herded thousands of sheep and oxen ahead, claiming tribute while clogging every lane so defenders could not sortie.

sentences.zh: 浚乃懼，或坐或起。

translations.literal: Jun then feared, sometimes sitting, sometimes rising.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun began to panic, pacing his seat.

sentences.zh: 勒升其廳事，命甲士執浚，立之-{于}-前，使徐光讓浚曰：「君位冠元臺，爵列上公，據幽都驍悍之國，跨全燕突騎之鄉，手握強兵，坐觀京師傾覆，不救天子，而欲自尊。

translations.literal: Le ascended his reception hall, ordered armoured soldiers to seize Jun, stood him in front, and sent Xu Guang to rebuke Jun, saying, "You, sir, rank foremost among ministers and hold highest duke rank; you occupy the fierce state of the You capital and stride the land of Yan's shock cavalry; you grasp strong troops yet sat watching the capital's collapse, did not rescue the Son of Heaven, and wished to exalt yourself." -{yu}-
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le mounted Wang Jun's dais, had guards drag him forth, and set Xu Guang to recite his crimes—power without loyalty while the throne burned -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 又專任姦暴，殺害忠良，肆情恣欲，毒遍燕壤。

translations.literal: Moreover you wholly employed treacherous cruelty, killed the loyal and good, indulged desire without restraint, and poison spread across the Yan soil.
translations.idiomatic: He let thugs rule, murdered loyalists, and poisoned every corner of Yan.

sentences.zh: 自貽-{于}-此，非為天也。

translations.literal: You brought this on yourself—it is not Heaven's doing." -{yu}-
translations.idiomatic: You earned this yourself—Heaven did not single you out." -{yu}-

sentences.zh: 」使其將王洛生驛送浚襄國市斬之。

translations.literal: He had his general Wang Luosheng escort Jun by post stages to Xiangguo market and behead him there.
translations.idiomatic: He shipped Wang Jun to Xiangguo market and took his head.

sentences.zh: 於是分遣流人各還桑梓，擢荀綽、裴憲，資給車服。

translations.literal: Thereupon he separately sent displaced people each back to their native villages, promoted Xun Chuo and Pei Xian, and supplied chariots and robes.
translations.idiomatic: He sent exiles home, raised Xun Chuo and Pei Xian, and gave them carriages and gowns.

sentences.zh: 數-{朱}-碩、棗嵩、田嶠等以賄亂政，責遊統以不忠-{于}-浚，皆斬之。

translations.literal: He impeached Zhu Shuo, Zao Song, Tian Jiao and others for taking bribes and disordering government, blamed You Tong for disloyalty to Jun, and beheaded them all -{zhu}- -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: He arraigned Zhu Shuo, Zao Song, and Tian Jiao for graft, condemned You Tong for betraying Wang Jun, and executed them all -{zhu}- -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 遷烏丸審廣、漸裳、郝襲、靳市等-{于}-襄國。

translations.literal: He moved the Wuhuan Shen Guang, Jian Shang, Hao Xi, Jin Shi and others to Xiangguo -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: He resettled Shen Guang, Jian Shang, Hao Xi, Jin Shi, and their Wuhuan bands at Xiangguo -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 焚燒浚宮殿。

translations.literal: He burned Jun's palaces.
translations.idiomatic: He torched Wang Jun's palaces.

sentences.zh: 以晉尚書劉翰為寧朔將軍、行幽州刺史，戍薊，置守宰而還。

translations.literal: He appointed Jin's former Minister Liu Han as general who calms the north, acting shepherd of Youzhou, to garrison Ji, set guards and magistrates, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He left Liu Han as acting Youzhou shepherd to hold Ji with a new garrison, then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 遣其東曹掾傅遘兼左長史，封王浚首，獻捷-{于}-劉聰。

translations.literal: He sent his eastern bureau clerk Fu You, concurrent left senior clerk, to seal Wang Jun's head and present victory to Liu Cong -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Fu You boxed Wang Jun's head for Liu Cong as proof of victory -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 勒旣還襄國，劉翰叛勒，奔段匹磾。

translations.literal: After Le had returned to Xiangguo, Liu Han rebelled against Le and fled to Duan Pidi.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shi Le was home, Liu Han bolted to Duan Pidi.

sentences.zh: 襄國大饑，穀二升直銀二斤，肉一斤直銀一兩。

translations.literal: Xiangguo suffered great famine: two sheng of grain cost two jin of silver; one jin of meat cost one liang of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Famine struck Xiangguo—two ladles of grain cost two pounds of silver, a pound of meat one tael.

sentences.zh: 劉聰以平幽州之勳，乃遣其使人柳純持節署勒大都督陝東諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、東單-{于}-，侍中、使持節、開府、校尉、二州牧、公如故，加金鉦黃鉞，前後鼓吹二部，增封十二郡。

translations.literal: Liu Cong, for the merit of pacifying Youzhou, then sent his envoy Liu Chun with staff to appoint Le grand commander of all military affairs east of Shan, general-in-chief of agile cavalry, Eastern Chanyu, palace attendant, bearer of credentials, opened office, colonel-in-chief, shepherd of two provinces, duke as before, added golden cymbals and yellow battle-axe, front and rear drum-and-pipe guards in two sections, increased enfeoffment by twelve commanderies -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong showered titles—grand commander east of Shan, swift-cavalry general-in-chief, Eastern Chanyu, opened office, twelve new commanderies, full regalia of a field marshal -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 勒固辭，受二郡而已。

translations.literal: Le firmly declined, accepting only two commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le refused most of it and kept two fiefs.

sentences.zh: 勒封左長史張敬等十一人為伯、子、侯，文武進位有差。

translations.literal: Le enfeoffed eleven men including left senior clerk Zhang Jing as earls, viscounts, and marquises; civil and military ranks advanced by degrees.
translations.idiomatic: He ennobled Zhang Jing and ten others and bumped ranks up and down the roster.

sentences.zh: 勒將支雄攻劉演於廩丘，為演所敗。

translations.literal: Le's general Zhi Xiong attacked Liu Yan at Linqiu and was defeated by Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Xiong struck Liu Yan at Linqiu and lost.

sentences.zh: 演遣其將韓弘、潘良襲頓丘，斬勒所署太守邵攀。

translations.literal: Yan sent his generals Han Hong and Pan Liang to raid Dunqiu, beheading Le's appointed prefect Shao Pan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan's men raided Dunqiu and killed prefect Shao Pan.

sentences.zh: 支雄追擊弘等，害潘良-{于}-廩丘。

translations.literal: Zhi Xiong pursued and struck Hong and the others, killing Pan Liang at Linqiu -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Xiong chased them down and killed Pan Liang at Linqiu -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 劉琨遣樂平太守焦球攻勒常山，斬其太守邢泰。

translations.literal: Liu Kun sent Leping prefect Jiao Qiu to attack Le's Changshan and beheaded his prefect Xing Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun's Jiao Qiu took Changshan and removed prefect Xing Tai.

sentences.zh: 琨司馬溫嶠西討山胡，勒將逯明要之，敗嶠-{于}-潞城。

translations.literal: Kun's marshal Wen Xi campaigned west against the mountain Hu; Le's general Lu Ming intercepted him and defeated Xi at Lucheng -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Xi marched against the hills; Lu Ming ambushed him at Lucheng -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 勒以幽冀漸平，始下州郡閱實人戶，戶貲二匹，租二斛。

translations.literal: Because You and Ji were gradually pacified, Le first ordered prefectures to audit households, levying two bolts of cloth per household and two hu of rent.
translations.idiomatic: With the north quieting, he ordered a census—two bolts and two hu per household.

sentences.zh: 勒將陳午以浚儀叛-{于}-勒。

translations.literal: Le's officer Chen Wu rebelled at Junyi against Le -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wu mutinied at Junyi against Shi Le -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 逯明攻甯黑-{于}-茌平，降之，因破東燕酸棗而還，徙降人二萬餘戶-{于}-襄國。

translations.literal: Lu Ming attacked Ning Hei at Chiping, subdued him, then broke Eastern Yan and Suanzao on the return, and moved more than twenty thousand surrendered households to Xiangguo -{yu}- -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ming crushed Ning Hei at Chiping, swept Eastern Yan and Suanzao, and moved twenty thousand captives to Xiangguo -{yu}- -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 勒使其將葛薄寇濮陽，陷之，害太守韓弘。

translations.literal: Le sent his general Ge Bo to raid Puyang, took it, and killed prefect Han Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Bo stormed Puyang and killed Han Hong.

sentences.zh: 劉聰遣其使人范龕持節策命勒，賜以弓矢，加崇為陝東伯，得專征伐，拜封刺史、將軍、守宰、列侯，歲盡集上。

translations.literal: Liu Cong sent his envoy Fan Kan with staff and edict to summon Le, bestowed bow and arrows, further honoured him as marquis east of Shan with sole authority to campaign, empowered him to appoint prefects, generals, magistrates, and rank marquises, all to be reported at year's end.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong sent Fan Kan with bows, arrows, and a patent making Shi Le eastern marquis with power to appoint officers and report yearly.

sentences.zh: 署其長子興為上黨國世子，加翼軍將軍，為驃騎副貳。

translations.literal: He appointed his eldest son Xing heir of the Shangduguo state, added general who supports the army, and made him second to the general-in-chief of agile cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He named his heir Shi Xing general of the supporting host and deputy to the swift-cavalry marshal.

sentences.zh: 劉琨遣王旦攻中山，逐勒所署太守秦固。

translations.literal: Liu Kun sent Wang Dan to attack Zhongshan and drive out Le's appointed prefect Qin Gu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun's Wang Dan cleared Zhongshan of prefect Qin Gu.

sentences.zh: 勒將劉勔距旦，敗之，執旦-{于}-望都關。

translations.literal: Le's general Liu Mian opposed Dan, defeated him, and captured Dan at Wangdu Pass -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian broke Wang Dan and took him alive at Wangdu Pass -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 勒襲邵續-{于}-樂陵。

translations.literal: Le raided Shao Xu at Leling -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: He fell on Shao Xu at Leling -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 續盡衆逆戰，大敗而還。

translations.literal: Xu led all his masses to meet him in battle, was greatly defeated, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Xu met him in the field, lost everything, and fled.

sentences.zh: 章武人王昚起-{于}-科-{斗}-壘，擾亂勒河間、渤海諸郡。

translations.literal: A man of Zhangwu, Wang Yin, rose -{yu}- at the Ke-{dou}- stockade and disturbed Hejian and Bohai commanderies under Le.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yin of Zhangwu seized the fort -{yu}- at Ke-{dou}- and raided Shi Le's Hejian and Bohai districts.

sentences.zh: 勒以揚武張夷為河間太守，參軍臨深為渤海太守，各率步騎三千以鎮靜之，使長樂太守程遐屯-{于}-昌亭為之聲勢。

translations.literal: Le made general who displays might Zhang Yi prefect of Hejian, adjutant Lin Shen prefect of Bohai, each leading three thousand foot and horse to quiet them, and ordered Changle prefect Cheng Xia to encamp at Changting to lend them weight -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zhang Yi and Lin Shen with three thousand riders each to pacify the zone and posted Cheng Xia at Changting to back them -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 徙平原烏丸展廣、劉哆等部落三萬餘戶-{于}-襄國。

translations.literal: He moved more than thirty thousand households of the Pingyuan Wuhuan Zhan Guang, Liu Duo and other tribes to Xiangguo -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: He resettled thirty thousand Wuhuan families from Pingyuan into Xiangguo -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 使石季龍襲乞活王平-{于}-梁城，敗績而歸。

translations.literal: He sent Shi Jilong to raid Qihuo Wang Ping at Liangcheng, was defeated, and returned -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jilong attacked Wang Ping's Qihuo band at Liangcheng, lost, and withdrew -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 又攻劉演-{于}-廩丘。

translations.literal: Again he attacked Liu Yan at Linqiu -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: He struck Liu Yan again at Linqiu -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 支雄、逯明擊甯黑-{于}-東武陽，陷之，黑赴河而死，徙其衆萬餘-{于}-襄國。

translations.literal: Zhi Xiong and Lu Ming struck Ning Hei at Dongwuyang, took him; Hei threw himself into the river and died; he moved his masses, more than ten thousand, to Xiangguo -{yu}- -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Xiong and Lu Ming stormed Dongwuyang, drove Ning Hei into the river, and shipped ten thousand survivors to Xiangguo -{yu}- -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 邵續使文鴦救演，季龍退止盧關津避之，文鴦弗能進，屯-{于}-景亭。

translations.literal: Shao Xu sent Wen Yang to relieve Yan; Jilong withdrew and halted at Luguan ford to avoid him; Wen Yang could not advance and encamped at Jingting -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Xu sent Wen Yang; Shi Jilong hugged Luguan to dodge him while Wen Yang stalled at Jingting -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 兗豫豪右張平等起兵救演。

translations.literal: Notables Zhang Ping and others of Yan and Yu raised troops to rescue Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Yan-Yu gentry led by Zhang Ping marched to save Liu Yan.

sentences.zh: 季龍夜棄營設伏-{于}-外，揚聲將歸河北。

translations.literal: Jilong by night abandoned camp and laid ambush outside, proclaiming he would return north of the river -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jilong faked a northward retreat and hid troops outside camp -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 平等以為信然，入-{于}-空營。

translations.literal: Ping and others believed it true and entered the empty camp -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ping swallowed the ruse and walked into the empty tents -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 季龍回擊敗之，遂陷廩丘，演奔文鴦軍，獲演弟啟，送-{于}-襄國。

translations.literal: Jilong turned back, struck and defeated them, then took Linqiu; Yan fled to Wen Yang's army; they captured Yan's younger brother Qi and sent him to Xiangguo -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jilong wheeled back, shattered them, took Linqiu, drove Liu Yan to Wen Yang, and sent captive Liu Qi to Xiangguo -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 演即劉琨之兄子也。

translations.literal: Yan was Liu Kun's elder brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan was Liu Kun's nephew.

sentences.zh: 勒以琨撫存其母，德之，賜啟田宅，令儒官授其經。

translations.literal: Because Kun had comforted and kept his mother alive, Le was grateful, granted Qi fields and houses, and ordered Confucian officials to teach him the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le, grateful that Liu Kun had sheltered Liu Yan's mother, gave Liu Qi land, tutors, and a mansion.

sentences.zh: 時大蝗，中山、常山尤甚。

translations.literal: At the time great locusts; Zhongshan and Changshan were worst.
translations.idiomatic: Locusts blotted Zhongshan and Changshan.

sentences.zh: 中山丁零翟鼠叛勒，攻中山、常山，勒率騎討之，獲其母妻而還。

translations.literal: Dingling Zhai Shu of Zhongshan rebelled against Le, attacked Zhongshan and Changshan; Le led horse to campaign, captured his mother and wife and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Shu of the Dingling rose; Shi Le rode out, seized his family, and came back.

sentences.zh: 鼠保-{于}-胥關，遂奔代郡。

translations.literal: Shu held out at Xuguan, then fled to Dai commandery -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Shu bolted for Xuguan, then ran to Dai -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 勒攻樂平太守韓據-{于}-坫城，劉琨遣將軍姬澹率衆十餘萬討勒，琨次廣牧，為澹聲援。

translations.literal: Le attacked Leping prefect Han Ju at Dian city; Liu Kun sent general Ji Dan with more than a hundred thousand to campaign against Le; Kun halted at Guangmu to sound support for Dan -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le besieged Han Ju at Dian while Liu Kun sent Ji Dan with a hundred thousand and hovered at Guangmu -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 勒將距之，或諫之曰：「澹兵馬精盛，其鋒不可發，宜深溝高壘以挫其銳，攻守勢異，必獲萬全。

translations.literal: Le's generals were about to oppose him; some remonstrated, saying, "Dan's soldiers and horses are keen and mighty; his edge must not be provoked—dig deep moats and raise high walls to blunt his keenness; offence and defence differ; thus you are sure to gain complete safety."
translations.idiomatic: Advisers urged walls against Ji Dan's fresh host.

sentences.zh: 」勒曰：「澹大衆遠來，體疲力竭，犬羊烏合，號令不齊，可一戰而擒之，何強之有！

translations.literal: Le said, "Dan's great host has come from afar; bodies are tired and strength spent; they are a flock of dogs and sheep without unified orders—can be captured in one battle—what strength is there!"
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le snorted that Ji Dan's tired rabble would break in one clash.

sentences.zh: 寇已垂至，胡可舍去，大軍一動，豈易中還！

translations.literal: The foe is already nearly upon us—how can we withdraw! Once the great army moves, is it easy to turn back mid-course!
translations.idiomatic: With the enemy on the doorstep retreat was suicide.

sentences.zh: 若澹乘我之退，顧乃無暇，焉得深溝高壘乎！

translations.literal: If Dan exploits our retreat, we will have no leisure—how then dig deep moats and high walls!
translations.idiomatic: Retreat would let Ji Dan ride them down—no time for siegework.

sentences.zh: 此為不戰而自滅亡之道。

translations.literal: This is the way to destroy oneself without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: That counsel meant slow death.

sentences.zh: 」立斬諫者。

translations.literal: He immediately beheaded the remonstrators.
translations.idiomatic: He executed the worriers on the spot.

sentences.zh: 以孔萇為前鋒都督，令三軍後出者斬。

translations.literal: He made Kong Chang vanguard commander-in-chief and ordered that any of the three armies who marched out late be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: He named Kong Chang vanguard and threatened late marchers with death.

sentences.zh: 設疑兵於山上，分為二伏。

translations.literal: He set feigned troops on the mountain and divided into two ambushes.
translations.idiomatic: He split ambushers on the heights.

sentences.zh: 勒輕騎與澹戰，偽收衆而北。

translations.literal: Le with light horse fought Dan, feigned gathering troops and fleeing north.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le skirmished with light horse then feigned flight north.

sentences.zh: 澹縱兵追之，勒前後伏發，夾擊，澹軍大敗，獲鎧馬萬匹，澹奔代郡，據奔劉琨。

translations.literal: Dan loosed his army in pursuit; Le's front and rear ambushers sprang together, struck from both flanks; Dan's army was greatly defeated; they took more than ten thousand suits of armour and horses; Dan fled to Dai commandery; Ju fled to Liu Kun.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Dan chased into the trap, lost ten thousand mounts, and fled toward Dai while Han Ju ran to Liu Kun.

sentences.zh: 琨長史李弘以幷州降-{于}-勒，琨遂奔-{于}-段匹磾。

translations.literal: Kun's chief clerk Li Hong surrendered Bingzhou to Le; Kun then fled to Duan Pidi -{yu}- -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hong handed Bingzhou to Shi Le, and Liu Kun bolted to Duan Pidi -{yu}- -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 勒遷陽曲、樂平戶-{于}-襄國，置守宰而退。

translations.literal: Le moved households of Yangqu and Leping to Xiangguo, set guards and magistrates, and withdrew -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: He relocated Yangqu and Leping families to Xiangguo and posted officials -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 孔萇追姬澹-{于}-桑幹。

translations.literal: Kong Chang pursued Ji Dan at Sanggan -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Chang ran Ji Dan down at Sanggan -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 勒遣兼左長史張敷獻捷-{于}-劉聰。

translations.literal: Le sent concurrent left senior clerk Zhang Fu to present victory to Liu Cong -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fu carried the victory tally to Liu Cong -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 勒之征樂平也，其南和令趙領招合廣川、平原、渤海數千戶叛勒，奔-{于}-邵續。

translations.literal: When Le had campaigned at Leping, the southern-he magistrate Zhao Ling had mustered several thousand households of Guangchuan, Pingyuan, and Bohai to rebel against Le and flee to Shao Xu -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: During the Leping campaign Zhao Ling rallied thousands to defect to Shao Xu -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 河間邢嘏累徵不至，亦聚衆數百以叛。

translations.literal: Xing Jia of Hejian, repeatedly summoned, did not come, and also gathered several hundred to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Jia of Hejian defied summons, raised hundreds, and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 勒巡下冀州諸縣，以右司馬程遐為寧朔將軍、監冀州七郡諸軍事。

translations.literal: Le inspected the counties of Jizhou below and appointed right marshal Cheng Xia general who calms the north and supervisor of military affairs for seven commanderies of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He toured Jizhou counties and made Cheng Xia overseer of seven Jizhou commanderies.

sentences.zh: 勒姊夫廣威張越與諸將蒱博，勒親臨觀之。

translations.literal: Le's brother-in-law Zhang Yue of Guangwei diced with generals; Le personally came to watch.
translations.idiomatic: His brother-in-law Zhang Yue gambled with generals while Shi Le looked on.

sentences.zh: 越戲言忤勒，勒大怒，叱力士折其脛而殺之。

translations.literal: Yue spoke jesting words that offended Le; Le was greatly angry, shouted for brawlers to break his shins and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: A careless joke cost Zhang Yue his legs and life.

sentences.zh: 孔萇攻代郡，澹死之。

translations.literal: Kong Chang attacked Dai commandery; Dan died there.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Chang took Dai; Ji Dan fell.

sentences.zh: 時司、冀、幷、兗州流人數萬戶在-{于}-遼西，迭相招引，人不安業。

translations.literal: At the time several tens of thousands of displaced households from Si, Ji, Bing, and Yan were in Liaoxi, summoning one another; people could not rest in their occupations -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of refugees from four provinces clustered in Liaoxi, unsettling the frontier -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 孔萇等攻馬嚴、馮䐗，久而不克。

translations.literal: Kong Chang and others attacked Ma Yan and Feng Zhu but long could not overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Chang besieged Ma Yan and Feng Zhu without success.

sentences.zh: 勒問計於張賓，賓對曰：「馮䐗等本非明公之深仇，遼西流人悉有戀本之思。

translations.literal: Le asked Zhang Bin for a plan; Bin replied, "Feng Zhu and others are not originally the enlightened lord's deep foes; the Liaoxi displaced all long to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin said Feng Zhu was no arch-enemy and exiles wanted to go home.

sentences.zh: 今宜班師息甲，差選良守，任之以龔遂之事，不拘常制，奉宣仁澤，奮揚威武，幽冀之寇可翹足而靜，遼西流人可指時而至。

translations.literal: Now it is fitting to recall the army and rest armour, select good guardians, assign them Gong Sui-style tasks without binding usual statutes, spread benevolent grace, display martial awe—then You-Ji raiders can be stilled with a lifted foot, and Liaoxi exiles can arrive in good time."
translations.idiomatic: Recall troops, post just magistrates, and the border quiets itself.

sentences.zh: 」勒曰：「右侯之計是也。

translations.literal: Le said, "The right marquis's plan is correct."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le agreed.

sentences.zh: 」召萇等歸，署武遂令李回為易北都護、振武將軍、高陽太守。

translations.literal: He summoned Chang and others back, appointed Wusui magistrate Li Hui as protector north of Yi, general who shakes might, and prefect of Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He recalled Kong Chang and named Li Hui to pacify the Yi north.

sentences.zh: 馬嚴士衆多李潛軍人，回先為潛府長史，素服回威德，多叛嚴歸之。

translations.literal: Many of Yan's soldiers had been Li Qian's troops; Hui had formerly been chief clerk in Qian's headquarters and always submitted to Hui's might and virtue; many rebelled Yan to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hui's old prestige peeled Ma Yan's ranks away.

sentences.zh: 嚴以部衆離貳，懼，奔-{于}-幽州，溺水而死。

translations.literal: Yan, because his host was divided, feared and fled to Youzhou, drowned in the water -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yan fled toward Youzhou and drowned -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 馮䐗率衆降-{于}-勒。

translations.literal: Feng Zhu led his masses to surrender to Le -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Zhu capitulated to Shi Le -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 回移居易京，流人降者歲常數千，勒甚嘉之，封回弋陽子，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: Hui moved to settle at Yijing; displaced who surrendered each year were often several thousand; Le greatly praised him, enfeoffed Hui as viscount of Yiyang with three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hui drew thousands of refugees yearly and earned a viscounty.

sentences.zh: 加賓封一千戶，進賓位前將軍，固辭不受。

translations.literal: He added a thousand households to Bin's fief and advanced Bin to forward general; Bin firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin refused added rank and fief.

sentences.zh: 河朔大蝗，初穿地而生，二旬則化狀若蠶，七八日而臥，四日蛻而飛，彌亙百草，唯不食三豆及麻，幷冀尤甚。

translations.literal: Great locusts on the Hebei plain; at first they bored from earth, in twenty days transformed like silkworms, in seven or eight days lay down, in four days moulted and flew, covering every herb; they did not eat only the three beans and hemp; Bing and Ji were worst.
translations.idiomatic: Apocalyptic locusts swept Bing and Ji but spared beans and hemp.

sentences.zh: 石季龍濟自長壽津，寇梁國，害內史荀闔。

translations.literal: Shi Jilong crossed from Changshou ford, raided Liang commandery, and killed interior secretary Xun Ge.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jilong crossed at Changshou, hit Liang, and killed Xun Ge.

sentences.zh: 劉琨與段匹磾、涉復辰、疾六眷，段末柸等會-{于}-固安，將謀討勒，勒使參軍王續齎金寶遺末柸以間之。

translations.literal: Liu Kun with Duan Pidi, She Fuchen, Jiulujuan, and Duan Moben met at Gu'an planning to campaign against Le; Le sent adjutant Wang Xu bearing gold and treasures to bribe Moben -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun mustered an alliance at Gu'an; Shi Le bribed Moben to wreck it -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 末柸旣思有以報勒恩，又忻於厚賂，乃說辰眷等引還，琨、匹磾亦退如薊城。

translations.literal: Moben both wished to repay Le's kindness and rejoiced in the rich bribe; then he persuaded Fuchen and Juan to withdraw; Kun and Pidi also retreated toward Ji city.
translations.idiomatic: Moben pocketed the gold and talked the Duan host home.

sentences.zh: 邵續使兄子濟攻勒渤海，虜三千餘人而還。

translations.literal: Shao Xu sent his elder brother's son Ji to attack Le's Bohai, captured more than three thousand persons and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Xu's nephew raided Bohai and took three thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 劉聰將趙固以洛陽歸順，恐勒襲之，遣參軍高少奉書推崇勒，請師討聰。

translations.literal: Liu Cong's general Zhao Gu submitted Luoyang in allegiance, feared Le would strike him, sent adjutant Gao Shao with letters exalting Le and begging troops to campaign against Cong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gu offered Luoyang yet feared Shi Le and begged him to march on Liu Cong.

sentences.zh: 勒以大義讓之，固深恨恚，與郭默攻掠河內、汲郡。

translations.literal: Le with great righteousness refused him; Gu deeply hated and, with Guo Mo, raided Henei and Ji commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le rebuffed him; Zhao Gu rampaged with Guo Mo.

sentences.zh: 段末柸殺鮮卑單-{于}-截附真，立忽跋鄰為單-{于}-。

translations.literal: Moben killed Xianbei Chanyu Jiefuzhen and set Hubalin as Chanyu -{yu}- -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Moben murdered Chanyu Jiefuzhen and raised Hubalin -{yu}- -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 段匹磾自幽州攻末柸，末柸逆擊敗之，匹磾奔還幽州，因害太尉劉琨，琨將佐相繼降勒。

translations.literal: Duan Pidi from Youzhou attacked Moben; Moben met him in battle and defeated him; Pidi fled back to Youzhou and thereupon killed Grand Commandant Liu Kun; Kun's generals and adjutants surrendered to Le in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Pidi struck Moben, lost, fled, murdered Liu Kun, and his officers went over to Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 末柸遣弟騎督擊匹磾-{于}-幽州，匹磾率其部衆數千，將奔邵續，勒將石越要之於鹽山，大敗之，匹磾退保幽州。

translations.literal: Moben sent his younger brother cavalry commander to strike Pidi at Youzhou; Pidi led several thousand of his host intending to flee to Shao Xu; Le's general Shi Yue intercepted him at Yanshan and greatly defeated him; Pidi withdrew to hold Youzhou -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Moben's brother chased Pidi; Shi Yue crushed him at Yanshan -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 越中流矢死，勒為之屏樂三月，贈平南將軍。

translations.literal: Yue was struck by a stray arrow and died; Le for him ceased music three months and posthumously invested him general who pacifies the south.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yue died to a stray shaft; Shi Le mourned three months.

sentences.zh: 初，曹嶷據有青州，旣叛劉聰，南稟王命，以建鄴懸遠，勢援不接，懼勒襲之，故遣通和。

translations.literal: Earlier Cao Yi held Qingzhou; having rebelled against Liu Cong, he submitted south to Jin orders; because Jiankang hung far and relief could not reach, he feared Le would raid him, therefore sent to open peace.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yi in Qingzhou played both sides against Jin distance and Shi Le's threat.

sentences.zh: 勒授嶷東州大將軍、青州牧，封琅邪公。

translations.literal: Le appointed Yi grand general of the eastern quarter and shepherd of Qingzhou, enfeoffed him duke of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le titled Cao Yi Qingzhou shepherd and duke of Langye.

sentences.zh: 劉聰疾甚，驛召勒為大將軍、錄尚書事，受遺詔輔政，勒固辭乃止。

translations.literal: Liu Cong grew gravely ill and by post summoned Le as grand general and recorder of the affairs of the masters of writing to receive testamentary edict as regent; Le firmly declined and therefore it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong tried to name Shi Le regent; Shi Le refused.

sentences.zh: 聰又遣其使人持節署勒大將軍、持節鉞，都督、侍中、校尉、二州牧、公如故，增封十郡，勒不受。

translations.literal: Cong again sent his envoy with staff to appoint Le grand general, staff and axe, commander-in-chief, palace attendant, colonel-in-chief, shepherd of two provinces, duke as before, adding ten commanderies; Le did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong piled titles; Shi Le waved them off.

sentences.zh: 聰死，其子粲襲偽位，其大將軍靳準殺粲-{于}-平陽，勒命張敬率騎五千為前鋒以討準，勒統精銳五萬繼之，據襄陵北原，羌羯降者四萬餘落。

translations.literal: Cong died; his son Can usurped the throne; his grand general Jin Zhun killed Can at Pingyang; Le ordered Zhang Jing to lead five thousand horse as vanguard to campaign against Zhun; Le commanded fifty thousand picked troops after him, occupying the plain north of Xiangling; Qiang and Jie who surrendered numbered more than forty thousand camps -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zhun slaughtered Liu Can; Shi Le marched on Pingyang with fifty thousand and camped north of Xiangling -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 準數挑戰，勒堅壁以挫之。

translations.literal: Zhun repeatedly challenged battle; Le held firm walls to blunt him.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zhun taunted; Shi Le sat tight.

sentences.zh: 劉曜自長安屯-{于}-蒲阪，曜復僭號，署勒大司馬、大將軍，加九錫，增封十郡，幷前十三郡，進爵趙公。

translations.literal: Liu Yao from Chang'an encamped at Puyang; Yao again assumed the imperial title, appointed Le grand marshal, grand general, added the nine bestowals, increased ten commanderies together with the prior thirteen commanderies, advanced the fief to duke of Zhao -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao proclaimed himself emperor and tried to buy Shi Le with the nine gifts and a Zhao dukedom -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 勒攻準-{于}-平陽小城，平陽大尹周置等率雜戶六千降-{于}-勒。

translations.literal: Le attacked Zhun at the lesser Pingyang city; grand steward of Pingyang Zhou Zhi and others led six thousand miscellaneous households to surrender to Le -{yu}- -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le pressed Pingyang's inner town until Zhou Zhi brought six thousand households over -{yu}- -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 巴帥及諸羌羯降者十餘萬落，徙之司州諸縣。

translations.literal: Ba chiefs and various Qiang and Jie who surrendered numbered more than a hundred thousand camps; he moved them to Si province counties.
translations.idiomatic: He relocated a hundred thousand Qiang-Jie captives into Henan counties.

sentences.zh: 準使-{卜}-泰送乘輿服御請和，勒與劉曜競有招懷之計，乃送泰-{于}-曜，使知城內無歸曜之意，以挫其軍勢。

translations.literal: Zhun sent Bu Tai to deliver imperial equipage and sue for peace; Le and Liu Yao each had plans to win them over; therefore he sent Tai to Yao to let him know the city had no mind to return to Yao, to blunt his army's momentum -{bu}- -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le shipped Bu Tai to Liu Yao to sow doubt -{bu}- -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 曜潛與泰結盟，使還平陽宣慰諸屠各。

translations.literal: Yao secretly allied with Tai, sent him back to Pingyang to console the various Tuge.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao smuggled a pact to Bu Tai.

sentences.zh: 勒疑泰與曜有謀，欲斬泰以速降之，諸將皆曰：「今斬-{卜}-泰，準必不復降，就令泰宣漢要盟-{于}-城中，使相率誅靳準，準必懼而速降矣。

translations.literal: Le suspected Tai and Yao had a plot and wished to behead Tai to hasten surrender; the generals all said, "Now if we behead Bu Tai, Zhun will surely not surrender again; yet if we let Tai proclaim Han's covenant in the city and lead them to kill Jin Zhun, Zhun will fear and surrender quickly." -{bu}- -{yu}-
translations.idiomatic: Generals argued killing Bu Tai would harden Jin Zhun -{bu}- -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 」勒久乃從諸將議遣之。

translations.literal: After long Le followed the generals' counsel and sent him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le reluctantly let Bu Tai go.

sentences.zh: 泰入平陽，與準將喬泰、馬忠等起兵攻準，殺之，推靳明為盟主，遣泰及-{卜}-玄奉傳國六璽送-{于}-劉曜。

translations.literal: Tai entered Pingyang, with Zhun's generals Qiao Tai, Ma Zhong and others raised troops attacking Zhun, killed him, pushed Jin Ming as covenant lord, sent Tai and Bu Xuan to deliver the six imperial seals to Liu Yao -{bu}- -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Bu Tai entered Pingyang, joined the coup against Jin Zhun, raised Jin Ming, and sent the jade seals toward Liu Yao -{bu}- -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 勒大怒，遣令史羊升使平陽，責明殺準之狀。

translations.literal: Le was greatly angry, sent clerk Yang Sheng as envoy to Pingyang, reproaching Ming for the circumstances of killing Zhun.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le raged and sent Yang Sheng to denounce Jin Ming for Jin Zhun's murder.

sentences.zh: 明怒，斬升。

translations.literal: Ming was angry and beheaded Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Ming executed the envoy.

sentences.zh: 勒怒甚，進軍攻明，明出戰，勒擊敗之，枕-{尸}-二里。

translations.literal: Le was extremely angry, advanced the army attacking Ming; Ming came out to battle; Le defeated him; corpses pillowing the road for two li -{shi}-.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le smashed Jin Ming's sortie and strewed two li with dead -{shi}-.

sentences.zh: 明築城門堅守，不復出戰。

translations.literal: Ming built the gates firm and held fast, no longer giving battle.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Ming slammed the gates and refused another field fight.

sentences.zh: 勒遣其左長史王脩獻捷-{于}-劉曜。

translations.literal: Le sent his left senior clerk Wang Xiu to present victory to Liu Yao -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiu carried the victory bulletin to Liu Yao -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 晉彭城內史周堅害沛內史周默，以彭沛降-{于}-勒。

translations.literal: Jin interior secretary of Pengcheng Zhou Jian killed interior secretary of Pei Zhou Mo and surrendered Peng and Pei to Le -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Jian murdered Zhou Mo and handed Pengcheng and Pei to Shi Le -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 石季龍率幽、冀州兵會勒攻平陽。

translations.literal: Shi Jilong led You and Ji troops to join Le attacking Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jilong marched You-Ji veterans to the Pingyang siege.

sentences.zh: 劉曜遣征東劉暢救明。

translations.literal: Liu Yao sent general of the east Liu Chang to relieve Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao dispatched Liu Chang to save Jin Ming.

sentences.zh: 勒命舍師-{于}-蒲上。

translations.literal: Le ordered to halt the army on the Pu upstream -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le stopped the host on the Pu heights -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 靳明率平陽之衆奔-{于}-劉曜，曜西奔粟邑。

translations.literal: Jin Ming led Pingyang's masses to flee to Liu Yao; Yao fled west to Suyi -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Ming bolted to Liu Yao, who then raced west to Suyi -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 勒焚平陽宮室，使裴憲、石會修復元海、聰二墓，收劉粲已下百餘-{尸}-葬之，徙渾儀、樂器-{于}-襄國。

translations.literal: Le burned Pingyang palaces and halls, sent Pei Xian and Shi Hui to repair the two tombs of Yuanhai and Cong, gathered more than a hundred corpses below Liu Can and buried them, moved the armillary sphere and ritual instruments to Xiangguo -{shi}- -{yu}-.
translations.idiomatic: He torched the Liu palaces, restored Liu Yuan and Liu Cong's tombs, buried the royal dead, and carted the observatory gear to Xiangguo -{shi}- -{yu}-.

sentences.zh: 劉曜又遣其使人郭汜等持節署勒太宰，領大將軍，進爵趙王，增封七郡，幷前二十郡，出入警蹕，冕十有二旒，乘金根車，駕六馬，如曹公輔漢故事，夫人為王后，世子為王太子。
